The Reputation: a stress roll of his Reputation against Ease Factor 6 (ArM5 p. 19) tells a character he prosecutes what others overlook and seeks the harshest penalty (p. 70). Tribunal records are open on a season's notice; Int + Code of Hermes, stress, Ease Factor 12, shows he wins by blackening the defendant's character with anecdotes barely tied to the case (p. 75). He investigated and prosecuted all his cases himself, which is unusual; most were settled at private hearing, so the full Tribunal never saw his methods; one or two challenges to his charging beyond the first complaint failed (pp. 75-76).

The powers of a Quaesitor (p. 72; Houses of Hermes: True Lineages pp. 61-66): he carries a letter of authority from the Primus and can lose it, and his House, for abuse; he must investigate serious complaints and may begin on his own; he may ask reasonable cooperation, which never includes submitting to magical interrogation; he may use magic in an investigation, but learning a magus's innocent affairs that way is a crime, softened by investigation immunity, under which he answers only for actual harm (True Lineages p. 62); he may call a March in an extreme case, for the Tribunal to ratify; he may not arrest or detain, nor order anyone to submit to mind-reading. Failure to cooperate is a low crime (p. 75).

Making him harder (p. 73): he is written with one fatal flaw, using spells on mundanes, to give the players a counter-claim. Let a grog do the legwork instead and the scrying charge goes away. Mundanes may testify in person or, more often, in writing, with magic used to see they speak freely; often Quaesitors use them only to find physical evidence (True Lineages p. 58).

Allies (p. 78): if the players start to feel the law is rigged, let a sympathetic magus he once savaged offer advice at a recess, such as the right to challenge evidence and demand its source. Well-wishers may turn up after the Tribunal whatever the verdict. Have a second player, with no magus on trial, play the presiding Quaesitor, coached on how seriously scrying is taken (p. 79).

Preparing the defense (p. 76): what a Quaesitor may do is mostly unwritten House tradition, and serving Quaesitors will not discuss a colleague's misconduct, so the answers may lie with experts outside the Tribunal or in distant libraries. The accused may call character witnesses, the best answer to his attacks on character. Make them easy to get: anyone the covenant has helped or lived at peace with should speak, and mundanes may too, with less weight. Reaching them opens side stories. Trial procedure is in True Lineages pp. 56-59 (p. 78).

neighbours.name: Baron Hugo's Castle
neighbours.summary: The seat of Baron Hugo, a nobleman of middling importance with authority in the area.
neighbours.secrets: Hannelore's work has spread an Infernal aura over the baron's lands and worn the castle's Dominion aura down to 1, so it fades entirely after dark (p. 88). The book names no strength for the Infernal aura here.

neighbours.name: Baron Hugo
neighbours.summary: A local nobleman of middling rank, whom the covenant will want to keep on good terms with. He loves his daughter Hannelore dearly, means to marry her to a wholesome and useful groom, and is disappointed that every match has failed. Little happens on his lands that he does not hear of.
neighbours.secrets:
He need not be a baron or landed: a knight or sheriff does as well, or an older brother or uncle who is her guardian. Whoever he is, he has a secret past (pp. 84, 86).

He owns books of Infernal Lore. Why is the storyguide's choice (p. 87): he was a sorcerer in youth who broke his staff and has lived blamelessly since, kept safe by a Faith point from a pilgrimage; or he belongs to a secret society within the Church against evil, run through an order such as the Templars, and keeps them as spoils to study the Enemy; or they are his wife's (see Lady Ermengarde); or an ancestor left them, he can barely read, and Hell has seen they stay with those who will use them.

As the story runs (pp. 88-89): depending on these he is ignorant or blinded by love, a pawn she forces, or a demon-hunter calling the magi in. Asked for help with proof and respect he is saddened but can believe it, given what he has seen. His price is her life spared, and he comes along to see to it. He supplies four soldiers (Standard Soldier, ArM5 p. 22) under a serjeant (Grizzled Veteran, ArM5 p. 21), perhaps a knight in residence, more in a day, and knowledge of the manor. He has probably the right of judge, jury and executioner over intruders.

neighbours.name: The Baron's Old Storage Caves
neighbours.summary: A run of caves once used by the baron's household to keep perishable food, since abandoned. They were enlarged long ago, dressed with stone, and go deep into the bedrock for the cool.
neighbours.secrets: Hannelore's hiding place. One cave is her ritual chamber, which holds the Infernal aura of 3; the aura is that cave's (p. 89).

neighbours.name: The Sulfurous Spring
neighbours.summary: A spring on the baron's estate that smells of sulfur.
neighbours.secrets: Once a year on Lammas Eve it belches forth vis, which the local witch coven has collected since time immemorial and Hannelore contests (p. 81).

neighbours.name: The Local Witch Coven
neighbours.summary: A coven of witches said to meet about the baron's estate.
neighbours.secrets: It has taken the sulfurous spring's Lammas Eve vis since time immemorial (p. 81). A stronger Hannelore takes over a coven of infernalists early on, for a Ceremony bonus (p. 84); younger siblings she corrupts could form hers instead (p. 86). The book gives no members.

neighbours.name: The Nunnery
neighbours.summary: An ordinary religious house with a solid foundation and high walls.
neighbours.secrets:
The book gives it no name. Establish it early in the saga, perhaps by having the characters guide lost novices there, so it seems an ordinary house (p. 91).

Hannelore is walled in here as an anchorite, fed through a hole. For an immediate escape it was corrupted before she came, by Father Fulke, and Hugo was steered to it by the demon; for a slow one it is in a state of grace and she brings it down (p. 91).

Most of it stays in the Dominion, but its aura weakens, an Infernal aura rises at night, and her cell's Dominion erodes until it no longer hinders her. Within months a few nuns make her comfortable; within a year she has grimoires and smuggled vis (pp. 91, 92).

Corrupted nuns are Initiated into her patron's Favored Abilities: Ceremony, Diablerie, Incantation, Malediction, Psychomachia. Each adds Presence + Incantation as a ceremonial bonus, and she leads one nun per point of Ceremony (RoP: Infernal p. 91); or in a leaderless ceremony 12 nuns and she add the sum of their Ceremony scores, less 13, on top (p. 91).

After she flies, her nuns cover for her and the prioress, ashamed, tells no one unless the magi stressed the danger. Her cell holds books on the maleficia and vis infesta, a crust of profaned Host that looks like Corpus vis to Hermetic magic; she took her vis prava (p. 91).

An attack on the nunnery must be utterly secret. Her patron warns the authorities, the walls keep people out and the Dominion hampers spells. If pressed she may burn it (p. 92).

neighbours.name: The Younger Nuns
neighbours.summary: A group of the younger nuns, lately rebellious and licentious.
neighbours.secrets: Hannelore's servants within the nunnery, won by her or by Father Fulke. Neither can corrupt the whole house, but their licence weakens its Dominion (p. 91).

neighbours.name: The Road Tavern
neighbours.summary: A tavern outside any town, by a busy road between two major towns, serving travellers. It is famed for its ale and a favourite of redcaps.
neighbours.secrets: Where Hannelore burns her enemies. The book gives it no name (p. 92).

neighbours.name: The Infatuated Diabolist
neighbours.summary: Baron Hugo's clever, wilful daughter has taken a liking to a magus of the covenant, and her father would not approve.

stages.title: A chance encounter
stages.clues: The characters meet Baron Hugo and his daughter of sixteen at a social occasion, perhaps part of another story: an ally's wedding, where the bride's family seems uncanny; a hunting party with a lunch and a tale of a fantastic beast; a feast for those who saved an important local. She fixes on a powerful male magus and invites him to try her new hawk, chaperoned.
stages.ignored: She pursues him anyway, sure she can win him.

stages.title: The affair
stages.clues: A love affair must stay secret: Hugo would never approve, and the covenant may fear a noble's wrath breaking the Oath. A lukewarm magus may be pushed by a faerie who kidnaps her and sends him a ransom demand, as a monster would in a story.
stages.ignored: She expects wooing he has no time for. Refused, she pesters, then turns petulant with blackmail or a noble's son defending her honour, small and easily handled, and seems to accept it. Outright rejection ends as badly. Hugo, hearing of it, breaks them up. Public scandal would sour the covenant's standing.

stages.title: Obsession and corruption
stages.clues: Rejected, she blames her lack of power; loved, she resents his absences and wants to share his work. She turns to her father's books. Over five years suitors sicken, have accidents, vanish or are found dead behind barred doors, and nobody can stand her company for long, not even Hugo.
stages.ignored: She waits until she thinks herself worthy of him.

stages.title: Hannelore woos her love
stages.clues: An invitation comes from Hugo, willing or forced, or a plea about demons, or her faked disappearance. At dinner she is calm. At night, once the Dominion fades, she comes to him in spirit, pours out her heart, then fades, leaving a foul sulfurous slime, and returns laughing. Intellego Vim shows Infernally tainted magic.
stages.ignored: He recoils: she screams and flees, seeking an Arcane Connection, then returns by surprise to bind him with Mother Lilith and The Scorched Heart, drains his Fatigue, and hides him from her father as a female companion. He may be her slave until his sodales come looking.
stages.turned: He plays along: she happily tells of the suitors she murdered and her dreams of killing her father. Social rolls of Ease Factor 6 or more keep her trusting, but every meeting risks a new Arcane Connection.

stages.title: Confronting Hannelore
stages.clues: The characters need the baron, who knows his lands and staff, to find her in the old caves. Without him he confronts them with armed men.
stages.stopped: They can outmatch her, but if he is not with them he arrives in time to stand between them and beg for her life; she may rush to his side and plead. If she dies here, skip to her final gambit.
stages.turned: He offers the nunnery, where as an anchorite she could do little harm and might repent. His goodwill may make the magi agree.

stages.title: Confinement and escape
stages.clues: Quick release keeps the tension; years away make an old enemy's return, and she may have gained experience, slower than before, with vis and profane reading. When she has nothing more to gain she flies out as a crow.
stages.stopped: Magi who go after her there, or strike by Arcane Connection, deserve reward. It robs the story of a showdown, so make her return as a ghost the more dramatic.

stages.title: The showdown
stages.clues: Each of her foes, and Hugo, gets a message seeming to come from an ally, naming a tavern.
stages.ignored: With all inside she bars the doors. An aethnicus (RoP: Infernal p. 67), bound by pact, lights the fire, and she follows it warding roof, doors and walls with Break Not, Bend Not. Clothed in the Dragon's Scales, she dances in the flames with a knife for any who get out, perhaps with demonic allies.
stages.stopped: Even Hugo now sees she must die. She may flee as a crow and be shot down, or call her father or love close to hear her confession and spit one last curse, offering herself as the sacrifice. Saving Hugo cements an alliance.

stages.title: Hannelore's final gambit
stages.clues: A year after her death a run of killings begins in her family, then among the baron's knights: wives slay husbands over infidelities and die soon after, or kill themselves. The deaths cluster around the anniversary. A character keeping up with the family or the local nobles may notice.
stages.ignored: She moves on to grogs and companions who helped her beloved. Thwarted and short of time, she goes straight for him, through possessed women if she must, wanting him to sin and die knowing who did it.
stages.stopped: A showdown on the anniversary, and angels of punishment drag her soul back to Hell in flame and smoke.

links.note: Vis she contests with the coven

neighbours.secrets:
Five years turn a spoiled girl into a powerful diabolist, still infatuated with a player character, and if she cannot have him no one shall. It shows both the perils of diabolists and their weakness: great strength given preparation, but none of a magus's ready firepower. Have Realms of Power: The Infernal to hand (pp. 7, 80).

Other kin (p. 86): brothers may avenge her honour; older sisters let Hugo indulge her refusing to marry; siblings, younger sisters above all, may form her coven.

A child (p. 90): if she consummates her lust with her beloved she may conceive, if he has no Longevity Ritual yet, or even if he is sterile with the help of an Infernal witch or demon (the Consumption Power). She may bear it hidden in the nunnery, for him to find after she escapes, or a child already born may move him to clemency. If it has the Gift it could be his apprentice; if Infernal powers helped, is it tainted?

The burning tavern (pp. 92-93). Smoke: Deprivation rolls (ArM5 p. 180) every 5 rounds, then every round; a wet cloth gives +3. Heat: a Short-Term Fatigue roll (ArM5 p. 178) each active round, -3 in mostly metal armour. Flames: +5 damage a round; metal armour stops protecting after 5 rounds; heroics may double to quadruple the base (ArM5 p. 181). After 10 rounds it is +10 and the roof may fall: each round a simple die at or under the rounds since it reached +10 brings +15 damage on everyone. Some two dozen panicking people are inside; Communication + Leadership, Ease Factor 12, gives some influence. Examples: a merchant offering silver to save his wares upstairs, a mother whose children are upstairs, lovers under a burning table, a local hero flinging ale at the fire.

The doors: Strength against Ease Factor 12. A charge costs a Short-Term Fatigue level and adds Athletics. Up to four may combine Strength to force, not to charge. A bench as a ram adds +3. An axe lies by the back door: each round a stress die +3 against Ease Factor 15, and failure, as printed, takes one of the door's 2 damage levels.

Timeline (p. 93). Round 1: Perception + Awareness, Ease Factor 12, to smell smoke, +3 by day with the cooking fire, +9 if asleep; all make a smoke Deprivation roll. Round 3: Ease Factor 6. Round 5: unmissable, Deprivation and Fatigue rolls every round. Round 10: fires everywhere, +5 a round. Round 15: +10 a round, door Ease Factor down 3, collapse possible.

neighbours.name: The Flagellants
neighbours.summary:
A penitential movement spreading from town to town, led by eloquent lay preachers. Its people pray, fast and call the world to repentance. Later they march in great processions behind banners that denounce human weakness, carrying whips and birch scourges, and in undyed robes with a red mark on the breast.

Its followers believe that their suffering is saving the world, and gladly say so to anyone who will listen. The sickness of recent years has passed them by.

details.rules: They call and answer in songs as they whip themselves, and at the name of Christ fling themselves to the ground.
details.wants: To expiate the sins of the world and end God's punishments.

neighbours.secrets:
Each cell's preacher thinks an angel chose him alone; the angel is Abaissier, an Angel of Punishment. Cells do not talk to each other, which is the cult's weakness, since Redcaps do. Questioned gently in many places and with the answers pooled, its members reveal its shape without ever noticing. A leader flattered in his spiritual Pride describes his visitor well enough for an expert in Infernal Lore to name the kind of demon.

Money and goods: at first members' own goods and alms; later extortion from towns and gifts from hidden patrons. Stocks were laid up for years, a sin in itself, and the processional crosses come from distant artisans, a first hint that the plot spans Europe. Unused caches can be destroyed. Tracing the goods names the nobles and churchmen who secretly support it; they will put themselves at the front of the crackdown and sabotage it.

Items. Uniforms: robes of wool or cotton given as alms by a nobleman in penance for a terrible crime, told to by an 'angel'; tracing them finds many local gathering points. False relics: Fabrico's, some breathing out the evil airs of plague, with an antidote for the flagellants. Blood-soaked rags: see the Open Heresy stage. Bufonia's 'holy oil', sprinkled on the rags. The Letter From an Angel: a false relic read out before a procession, which eases its way past obstacles and whose symbols Fabrico marks on things to order them destroyed, held or venerated.

Truly pious flagellants exist, monks and even saints among them. Moderate, voluntary flagellation or one set by a bishop is allowed when treated as punishment or as a way to fix the attention, not as earning merit; penance in place of atonement is not. Abaissier tries to trick his enemies into attacking such people. Those spared can dispute with the leaders and bring followers back to the Church.

neighbours.name: The False Saints
neighbours.summary: Flagellant leaders hailed as men returned from the dead, who ordain their own priests outside the Church. Some shelter with noblemen already on poor terms with the bishops.
neighbours.secrets:
Their deaths and returns are elaborate waking dreams worked by Abaissier and Fabrico, given to one leader in each region so that each thinks himself uniquely blessed. Once false priests are ordained the Church turns on these groups, with arms if needed.

Finding one means learning where he hides and passing his guards: noblemen, possessed followers, or animals tainted by demons without his knowing. A pious character can win one over on a contested roll of stress die + Communication + Theology against his Pride, beating him by at least 6; showing him that demonic animals guard him adds 6. The penitent may enter a monastery or nunnery, though some bishops will want him dead, or find work with the Order.

neighbours.name: The Loyal Flagellants
neighbours.summary: Flagellant groups that denounce the false saints and keep the support of part of the Church. Some nobles follow them and make war on those who shelter the saints, and parts of the Order favour them.
neighbours.secrets:
Their opposition is a strategic pose that survives the purge and lets Abaissier go on training heretics for some years.

Ways to prove it. Bring Church witnesses to one of the secret meetings between senior members of the two halves. Capture one of the very few 'loyal' men the demons have told are saints: put to the question, he is too Proud to keep up the lie. Help the nobleman who has had a false angel and also a true vision of the Archangel Michael: he attacks lords of the 'loyal' side while rivals in disguise muster with the false saints, and if he wins he can take them, or their bodies, to the Church as proof.

neighbours.name: The Abandoned Building
neighbours.summary: An abandoned building in the district.
neighbours.secrets:
The manufactory of bloodied rags. Flagellants take turns whipping themselves here, sitting on a floor spread with filthy bed sheets. Each evening an acolyte cuts the sheets into palm-sized pieces, which are carried off, sprinkled with 'holy oil' and smuggled to supporters in nearby towns.

If it is attacked, bodiless demons possess the acolytes, help them fight and move their bodies after death. The book sets it in the covenant's local area, and prints no aura.

neighbours.name: The Rise of the Flagellants
neighbours.summary: Lay preachers of unusual eloquence are appearing across the region, and prophets are foretelling the Antichrist and the end of the world.

stages.title: Cells of Flagellants
stages.clues: A man known for his eloquence turns lay preacher; Abaissier seduces at least six such. Fabrico's separate prophets of the end make people ready to listen. The first meeting is one cult member in a story about something else.
stages.ignored: Seed: a senior bandit says an angel told him to leave sinners, helps the characters ambush his old band, and goes off to preach; he may return as a flagellant.
stages.turned: Seed: Abaissier destroys a cell whose leader proselytizes too soon, to keep the Church's eyes off. Assailed by Hell, the cell looks holy, and survivors given positions of trust are later contacted as his agents.

stages.title: Shock to the Community
stages.clues: Crops fail, whether naturally or by raiders, small demons rotting seed corn and arsonists. Bufonia's minions pour poison in city wells, and plague comes. Mortal puppets spread leaders' venal sins and forged crimes. Public flagellants, untouched by the plague, appear across a wider area, asking only prayer and fasting; some gatherings raise brief Dominion auras.
stages.ignored: Communities lose heart and blame God's displeasure. Characters may exploit the rumours against rivals.
stages.stopped: Seeds: magi feed nearby towns by magic or wealth and hunt the local causes of harm, though few will link them to Abaissier yet. Stopping the well-poisoners lets the plague burn out; smeared potentates may want rumours traced or need mediating. Destroying Malicia here slows the cult.

stages.title: Processions Begin
stages.clues: Pilgrims march with whips and scourges still unused, under banners of threat on God's behalf. Fights break out at the edges.
stages.ignored: Unopposed, the processions gain popularity.
stages.stopped: Opposed, the marchers grow furious and think worldly powers corrupt. Local priests answer with processions for local saints.
stages.turned: Seed: Infernal disruptions hit the counter-processions, with possessed attackers, loose herds, impassable roads and fires. Those who protect them earn a good Reputation with the priests likeliest to lead the fight.

stages.title: Spread of the Cult
stages.clues: Waking dreams, visitations, bards and pilgrims carry the ideas, and Redcaps, alarmed at how many places they start from, tell friendly covenants. Rival bands fight in the streets. Seers report a battle of powers. Flagellants near the covenant take up uniforms.
stages.ignored: Fabrico claims part of the movement and the two demons fight until one makes the other a vassal; the book expects Abaissier to win.
stages.stopped: Seed: assassination, prison, disputation, smears or cutting off resources reduce local leaders. So can passing their names to moderate churchmen, who hold them apart from their followers, or to nobles they have mocked.

stages.title: Larger Processions
stages.clues: Marches last 33.5 days, a day for each year of Christ's life, and reach a thousand of both sexes and all ages. False miracles are talked of. Flagellant songs appear, and marchers grow proud of their filthy robes and skip Sunday services.
stages.ignored: Superabundant suffering: some think their whipping excuses other crimes. Seed: a noble seizes a widow and her lands by rape and forced marriage, his guards using peasants as shields and digging up babies' corpses to spread terror. Intervening wins the widow as an ally. Other flagellant nobles, first to question the Church, may suit covenants on bad terms with it.
stages.stopped: Seed: funnier ballads (stress die + Communication + a suitable Ability, 15+) outrun the songs, or bards are paid, jailed or killed. Magic items that remove songs from memory help; Quaesitores and Redcaps hold a few, and Quaesitores need more convincing to lend.

stages.title: Inadvertent Sins
stages.clues: Sickness follows long pilgrimages, late enough for the flagellants to claim they held it off. Some of the Church still backs them; most know something is wrong. Counter-processions grow and are sabotaged, and flagellants think whipping pays for that too.
stages.ignored: Fabrico's relics carry plague down the roads. In the nearest city a pro-flagellant faction plans to open the gates, riot and overthrow its rulers; if shut out, Bufonia's students poison the wells to discredit the rulers. Elsewhere the pious, aided by saints, resist, in riots, battles or de facto sieges.
stages.stopped: Seed: spreading word that the processions herald plague makes towns shut their gates. Characters can infiltrate the fifth column, catch the poisoners, purify wells or find other water, and find a cure for Fabrico's vapours or Bufonia's toxin. Dupes may drop concoctions or false relics in water to protect their town.

stages.title: Open Heresy
stages.clues: Knowing God will end the cult, Abaissier pushes it to do all the harm it can and gives Fabrico free rein. Flagellation is held to replace the sacraments, and to pass its virtue to others, so the rich buy forgiveness, which is simony. Leaders work miracles, only outside towns, since the Dominion there is too strong. Rags and a Letter From an Angel appear. Some leaders 'die and rise'.
stages.ignored: A woman, most often, who makes a rag herself and wipes the blood in her eyes thinks she has holy sight. It opens a hole in her defences: demons use Evocation on her, resisted by a Personality roll of 9+. Rags may carry plague, and Bufonia has them dropped in wells and granaries. False saints begin ordaining, and all Church support for them ends.
stages.stopped: Seeds: a merchant burns rivals' shops and keeps three flagellants in a woodland cottage to forgive him; their families gossip. Another puts ergot and chalk in bread, and criminals know him as a bulk buyer. Grogs patrol for rags and neighbourhood watches drive off spreaders. The manufactory can be found and destroyed. Fewer leaders means each works miracles more often, and demons cannot be everywhere, so strike several false prophets at once; a big alliance will probably be noticed by a minor demon. A cult shattered here makes the region a centre of resistance, a crusaders' staging area spared invasion, and the covenant's influence can shield a few others.
stages.turned: Seed: with an original letter and its materials, forgers (Intelligence + Finesse or Dexterity + Craft, 9+) can send a group anywhere, since not even a visited leader can overrule God's own letter. He obeys more zealously if the tone stokes his Pride. Fabrico will notice, and may hide it from Abaissier if the magi seem useful against him.

stages.title: Flagellant Civil War
stages.clues: Some groups oppose the false saints and keep Church backing. Nobles take sides, some on each, and parts of the Order support the 'loyal' flagellants. Crusaders march on the false saints.
stages.ignored: The purge spares the loyal half, and Abaissier goes on training heretics for years.
stages.stopped: Killing or detaining a false saint shifts the Church's attention elsewhere. Proving the split a pose destroys the rest of the cult, and may bring Abaissier down on those who prove it.

stages.title: Resurrecting the Cult
stages.clues: Remnants of broken cells are told they passed God's test, and new secret societies form from them, together or apart.
stages.ignored: The cycle begins again, and the demons may feud anew when Abaissier finds Fabrico's cults.
stages.stopped: Handled personally, the cells give leads to confront the demons. Reported, the Church destroys them and ties with it grow. The demons may then treat the characters as enemies, avoid them, or both.

neighbours.secrets:
Three demons who usually work alone happen to be active in one region. Demons cannot truly be patient or share, so this is no plan: each sets its minions going, and the humans, who can scheme, find their own mischief. Left alone the cult kills thousands, ruins the region's economy and leaves Infernal auras behind. A storyguide need not use every stage, but should plant the motifs of any skipped.

Why magi must care. The Church or the Divine will end the heresy, but not gently: preachers first, then armies, and an invasion is an invasion to a covenant's farmers and merchants. Crusaders also strike at Jews, Muslims, pagans and problem people with fortresses, and a younger son who takes a heretic's castle may keep it, so beaten raids do not deter them. Infernal auras left behind seed later trouble.

Any stage. Abaissier may trick the characters into attacking the truly pious. His movement also wrecks other demons' plots, so a storyguide who wants it harder may have him suborn them as fractious lieutenants. Rival bands fall out, and helping one side yields the other's secrets, which are much the same.

Research. Infernal Lore can find earlier flagellant heretics, but naming a demon from the Order's usual sources is very hard. Specialists can spot Abaissier and foresee the early stages, until he and Fabrico join and the precedent breaks; the uniforms then make him easy to identify.

Ending it. Goad Abaissier into battle, or draw out Fabrico. Dispute with the charismatic dupes: if they are humbled and reconciled the cult crumbles. Relieve the famine and disease that feed it, and prove the prophecies false. A big enough lie may do it, a false miracle saying God is satisfied and sending people back to the Church. Comedy works too: one historical revival died when the laity of Rome laughed at its marchers.

neighbours.name: The Abbey of the Reclusive Abbot
neighbours.summary:
A remote abbey of good craftsmen, known for its charity, its fairs and its pigeon lofts. Its church-building and seasonal fairs bring work to the country round it, and the prior deals with outsiders, since the abbot keeps to his bed after driving off a dragon at great cost to his health.

Visitors are kept to a small, detached part of the grounds. The scriptorium's windows are sealed with parchment, and the library is closed.

links.note: On a task for the abbot

neighbours.secrets:
The abbot is the dragon. Only a few monks know; three or four senior brothers run the house and tell the rest he has visions on his sickbed (use the priest, ArM5 p. 23, or Brother Julian, Art & Academe p. 85). The archdeacon may be among those who revere it. No one lies for it: they say the abbot cannot come or dine, and the prior stands in.

The aura is Divine 4 or 5 in the abbey and scriptorium (p. 118). The order is the troupe's: the book says friars and monks loosely, and no order of 1220 has both, so decide at the start of the saga (p. 109).

If discovery nears, the abbot 'dies', and a trusted elder or the prior is elected to front for it while it hides nearby or in the cellars. If nobles push in a new abbot, the monks do not contest it, but work to bring him into the fold.

Relics and items (p. 113): Ancient Magic oddities such as Canaanite clay tablets, defixio plates, fetish figures or pieces of automata; texts about them; practical Hermetic devices of at most three magnitudes, for moving stones or clearing brush; and small relics such as thorns of the Crown, scraps of Christ's robe, slivers of the True Cross or saints' bones. It uses what it safely can for the people, as tools of God, then gives relics to the bishop after parading them; what it cannot use it destroys or locks away.

A band's leader may carry a small relic giving a little Magic Resistance, and bands take four pigeons, two to send for help, one after two nights, and one kept for an attack.

neighbours.name: Jerusalem
neighbours.summary: Named as a distant pilgrimage goal for the devout.

neighbours.name: Sea of Galilee
neighbours.summary: Named as a distant pilgrimage goal for the devout.

neighbours.name: St Catherine's Monastery
neighbours.summary: At Mount Sinai, with a great library; named as a distant pilgrimage goal for the devout.

neighbours.name: Santiago de Compostela
neighbours.summary: At the end of the Way of St. James in Spain; named as a distant pilgrimage goal for the devout.

neighbours.name: Canterbury Cathedral
neighbours.summary: In England; named as a distant pilgrimage goal for the devout.

neighbours.name: The Abbey's Good Works
neighbours.summary: The abbey's generosity is changing the country around it: new and mended churches, fairs, paid apprenticeships, repairs to plough and wagon. Vis sites seem to yield less, and folk of the old places grow uneasy.

stages.title: Conflict Over Vis
stages.clues: The magi reach a vis site to find a recent camp and a plain trail to monks resting at an inn, with vis from several sites, some unknown to them or owned by other covenants.
stages.ignored: The monks go home with the vis. They refuse politely; coerced, they take sanctuary in the church, send a peasant as decoy, and release pigeons for help.
stages.stopped: The storyguide decides ahead what rescue comes: the dragon itself, a devoted knight, or none, so it can study the aftermath. Other magi may arrive for their vis, with certamen or murder in mind. Those who kill monks become the abbot's targets, and other covenants may fall to show its power.
stages.turned: However it ends, Rasa eats the pigeons and learns who was there and what they did.

stages.title: A Spiritual Encounter
stages.clues: A thinking faerie or magical nature spirit, too weak for the Aegis, asks to speak with the magi: the abbey's growing aura will overrun its home. It offers a vis site, an alliance or treasure.
stages.ignored: It turns to other covenants or to outlaws, whose harassment brings the lord and the Quaesitor around.
stages.turned: Townsfolk are building a church and graveyard on its glade, cutting the standing stone into a cross. A cheerful friar with a noble's soldiers tells of a bell and a saint's relic to come.

stages.title: The Friars Approach
stages.clues: A rich man dies without heirs and leaves the abbey money, with the bishop's approval, to rebuild a church in or near the covenant's grounds. If the covenant has a church, the monks offer to improve it, or Rasa 'accidentally' burns it in a storm. Representatives come with a writ, backed by bishop and nobles.
stages.ignored: Friars ask a rich covenant for money, or offer a poor one more buildings, apprenticeships and tax help for labour, and a new congregation grows at the door.
stages.stopped: A forged heir, a talk with the bishop, or sabotage confuses the friars, who won't fight but tell the abbot, and its attention follows.

stages.title: Failing Resources
stages.clues: The old, friendly abbey now closes its doors. Rumour says the abbot drove off the dragon and lies abed. New building begins and friars go abroad.
stages.ignored: Craft and library are lost to the covenant, and the Divine aura goes on spreading from the abbey.
stages.stopped: This story most easily reveals the truth. The battlefield may hold Arcane Connections, scrying may glimpse the dragon, and a friar on the road may talk.
stages.turned: Rasa may offer a bargain: its wisdom for help gathering relics and vis, with a share of the salvage. Its demands grow, its aura nears the covenant, and an ally becomes a close foe.

stages.title: The Traitor Within, The Traitor Without
stages.clues: A monk who found out what the abbot is flees to the magi, sure a beast that ate a saint must serve Hell, with descriptions, Arcane Connections or wrong plans.
stages.stopped: He may stay and advise or go back as an inside man.
stages.turned: Or the dragon cultivates him unknowing, to feed the magi lies and bring them out where it can destroy them without collateral damage. It may think them Infernal agents.

stages.title: The Lord's Bargain
stages.clues: The abbey's hold on labour and goods frustrates the local nobility. A clever lord, or one the covenant has dealt with, seeks the magi against this secretive, incorruptible, ever more popular abbot.
stages.ignored: He offers limited autonomy or relief from feudal dues in return for quiet action, a hard offer to turn down.
stages.turned: Once they accept, he won't take failure and threatens civil punishment. Reckless magi may be charged at Tribunal as court wizards to a mundane lord, and must find a Quaesitor to speak for them or defend themselves, while the abbot's power grows.

neighbours.secrets:
A long-term foe with no wish for open conflict. It remakes the covenant's world instead: as the Divine aura climbs, Magic and Faerie ones fade and vis fails. Run it behind another arc, using all four first stories in order, with two or three of the main arc's stories between each. The book's example braids it with Baron Geoffroi (p. 113). Treat these as stages of one slow rise, ending when the troupe notices or the storyguide chooses, when it becomes the main arc.

Works. Relics found from memory are paraded to build faith, then given to the bishop. Hoard money rebuilds churches, bridges, walls and wells, opens missions and pays for seasonal fairs at the abbey (City & Guild p. 106), quietly refunding peasants' table fees. Apprentices sponsored go home and enrich their regions.

How magi notice. Quaesitores and Hoplites may come asking, magi at the edge of their powers notice it first, or Tribunal assigns it. Faeries seek out the cause and may offer alliance. Demons driven off look for sinful grogs and covenfolk, possessing them past the Aegis or harassing them outside it. Failing vis sets covenants against each other in certamen and at Tribunal, which argues the effect and not the cause. Masons and craftsmen won't work for anyone but the abbey; grogs take vows and crusade, covenfolk go on pilgrimage, scholars shun the covenant, and loaned books vanish into the abbey.

The soft way. Win its trust and talk it into leaving: a pilgrimage to Jerusalem or the Sea of Galilee, St Catherine's on Sinai, Santiago by the Way of St. James, Canterbury, or a far hermitage. It stays there, and people from that place may later come asking where it came from. Or persuade it to sacrifice itself for its flock against Mongols, Crusaders or a Moorish or Arab host, with gathered proof of such armies' cruelty.

The hard way. A frontal attack is near hopeless, given its Might, the aura and the consequences of assaulting a house of God. Hurt its supports instead. Ambush travelling clergy, at a cost in nerve and reputation. Impersonate monks to disgrace them, risking confession. Turn the Church on them with charges of heresy or crimes, or expose what it is, since it is not even human. Blight crops and stock, for instance Wizard's Autumn (PeHe 15), a moon-long salting of the earth (CrTe 15: Base 3, +1 Touch, +3 Moon), Clouds of Rain and Thunder or Clouds of Summer Snow (CrAu 25), or Curse of the Ravenous Swarm (CrAn 45); destroy a flock's wool (PeAn 15: Base 3, +2 Voice, +2 Group); or stop milk and eggs (PeAn 25: Base 5, +2 Voice, +2 Group). Spoil trade, for instance with Pains of Perpetual Worry (CrMe 20), Panic of the Trembling Heart (CrMe 15) or a moon-long Recollection of Memories Never Quite Lived (MuMe 5), or tip off bandits. A dragonslayer or another dragon may do the fighting. With Arcane Connections gathered and the dragon drawn out of its aura, magi stand a good chance.

The enemy of my enemy. Another covenant, demons, an archbishop, the whole Tribunal or faeries may do the deed, but each leaves consequences: Quaesitores stay, clergy start purges, demons stay on, and faeries may turn from heroes to despots.

neighbours.name: The Land of Gold and Glass
neighbours.summary: A kingdom in the faerie lands, reached by way of mirrors, where every familiar thing of the mortal world has its counterpart in warped glass.
neighbours.secrets:
The completed Frame of Gold, set between two mirrors, is a corridor here (Ant p. 124). Raiders meet the Undistinguished Warriors, and at the last the Distinguished Knight (pp. 130-131). The book prints no aura for the kingdom itself; where the Queen extends it by Extend Glamour, the area has a Faerie aura of 6 (p. 122).

Faerie Lore of 21+ tells of this kingdom and of its entry by mirrors (p. 129).

neighbours.name: The Court of Gold and Glass
neighbours.summary:
Old tales speak of a faerie queen whose servants come and go by mirrors, each one a reflection of some real person, the very pattern of a place in human society.

Her badge is the mirror. It may be worn, sewn, carried or painted on an inn sign.
neighbours.ruler: The Queen of Gold and Glass

details.rules:
The Distinguished are the Queen's finished servants, one to each role: Pretenses of 9 in what the role needs, nothing in its lesser tasks, and a symbolic object holding vis deep in the head (Ant pp. 129-130).

The Undistinguished are unfinished: Pretense 6, Might 5 to 20, pieces of the body missing or see-through, but a flawless human face. None can break a mirror or attack anyone who carries one (p. 130).

The Hazy Servants have no fixed role and the Shadowy Minions are hardly there at all (pp. 130-131).

neighbours.secrets:
The Queen wants a court magician: faeries who cast as real magi cast, wear what they wear and sound as they sound (Ant p. 120).

The Queen will ransom a Distinguished Servant as a mortal monarch would, and is loath to lose one, but spends it if that draws out interesting spells. Many have External Vis, so a defeat in battle seldom ends them. Given a ready replacement, she does not care (Ant p. 130).

Highly cognizant faeries such as the Queen can redesign their lesser faeries; the book gives this no Virtue, but this story rests on it (p. 121). She uses human hirelings, dupes and captured monsters as well, because her faeries' powers are alike and would draw out too few kinds of spell (p. 124).

Smoothfaces and knockers are no part of the court, but both scorn mirrors (pp. 127, 129).

neighbours.name: The Cursed Mirror of the Artisan
neighbours.summary: A flawless mirror made for a faithless lover in the days of Rome's first advance, then cursed and put in the ground.
neighbours.secrets: A faerie dug it up and gave it to the princess, and through it the Queen took her (Ant p. 120). The book does not say where it is now, or whether it is the mirror of the heart.

neighbours.name: The Heart-Shaped Mirror
neighbours.summary: Gold-backed glass in the shape of a heart, in whose depths a woman can be seen.
neighbours.secrets: The largest piece of the Queen's body when she dies. Characters can reach in and draw out the princess, which shatters it; the shards hold 8 pawns of Imaginem in all. This is a decoy, not her anchor (Ant p. 123).

neighbours.name: The Gold and Glass Bead
neighbours.summary: A bead of gold and glass, the dearest possession of the woman who wears it.
neighbours.secrets: The Queen's spirit is anchored here, with 8 pawns of vis (no Art printed). Wearing it works as Aura of Rightful Authority. Unless this vis is harvested, she may in time move to another object or rebuild her body (Ant p. 123).

neighbours.name: Gold-Backed Mirrors
neighbours.summary:
Rome made its mirrors of glass with gilded backs. Nobody in Mythic Europe still does, unless perhaps some magus who keeps the old imperial crafts. Today's mirrors are steel, silver, polished marble and, here and there, glass backed with lead.

So a mirror of any sort is scarce and costly, and one backed in gold stands out.
neighbours.secrets: The Queen's name comes from them (Ant p. 123). Awareness rolls about these mirrors are +3 easier (Ant p. 129). A minion who takes a symbolic object for her must in time be shown as hers, by the mirror (p. 122).

neighbours.name: A Bonisagus Account
neighbours.summary: A centuries-old record by a long-dead magus of House Bonisagus.
neighbours.secrets: It tells of the Queen's earlier attempt to make a faerie skilled in the Arts for her courtier. Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore against an Ease Factor of 15 recalls or finds it. If the storyguide wishes, the roll also points to The Rare Book (Ant p. 129).

neighbours.name: The Rare Book
neighbours.summary: A rare book.
neighbours.secrets: It describes the Queen's powers and weaknesses. Held, by bad luck, at a reclusive covenant far away. Getting to it makes a separate story, connected but with a different theme (Ant p. 129). Neither covenant nor book is named.

neighbours.name: A Run of Odd Troubles
neighbours.summary: Odd troubles come to the covenant, years apart, with no enemy to show for them.

stages.title: Marked as her protagonists
stages.clues:
A notable meeting with one of her minions, memorable enough that the magi can later name it as the start. She stays out of sight. A mirror about the minion marks it as hers, though it need not be stressed: embroidered on a surcoat, jumbled in a pocket, or painted on an inn sign (Ant pp. 121-123).

Examples (pp. 123-124): a faerie smith mends a magic item for the council's decanter, or a faerie knight fights a demon at the magi's side and asks a spent Aegis token. A sprite risks itself to steal something trivial marked with the covenant's sigil, outside the Aegis. A faerie bard offers a game of riddles or a wager, the stake being one chosen word the losers never say again; winnings only lead to more of her servants. A faerie hostess swears not to harm her guests and then takes their bathwater and beard stubble to her mistress. A country lad, sent to fish a year downstream and bring in what he draws up, nets hair from the covenant's refuse.
stages.ignored: She needs symbolic objects for each magus: Arcane Connections, or anything that stirs them strongly, or items of the covenant that serve for all its members. She can make Arcane Connections by speech and gifts of food, and shape these into symbolic objects that never fade (p. 122).

stages.title: Animal: The Plague of Animals
stages.clues: Hazy Servants loose small beasts foreign to the area, which ruin its farming. Some, of a different colour, hold a little vis; others are huge and fierce, even of gentle kinds, and hold none. The Distinguished Huntsman comes after the huge ones and seems a rival for the vis (Ant p. 125).
stages.ignored: The common beasts are wholly natural and can migrate through the Aegis. The vis-bearing ones have Might and the giants carry a spell-like effect, so those cannot cross it.
stages.stopped: She hopes for conjured predators, magical pens and direct destruction, to steal. A piece of the frame may lie deep in one of the larger beasts.

stages.title: Aquam: Unprecedented Flood
stages.clues: Mirrors on the bed of a great river let its water out through shiny things in a small town near the covenant (Ant p. 125).
stages.ignored: The longer the land stays soaked, the worse for crops and buildings. Her powers hardly pierce the Aegis, so trickles from shiny things in the covenant do no direct harm, but water once moved is natural and seeps in from outside.
stages.stopped: Smash the reflective surfaces, some hard to reach against the force of the water, and then deal with what remains. A piece of the frame may be in a huge sturgeon stranded at the high-water mark.

stages.title: Auram: Sickening Vapors
stages.clues: A nearby village falls sick. The foul air comes up a well, sent by mirror from a far-off swamp (Ant pp. 125-126).
stages.ignored: The cloud settles over the village and its corners.
stages.stopped: A cover stops it, since the well's surface does not reflect in the dark. Magi can treat the sick and raise winds to clear the cloud. For good: cover it so that light never falls on the water, cast a spell with that effect, take the frame piece from the sediment, or let down an unbroken mirror.

stages.title: Corpus: People are Corpus, Too
stages.clues: Money, not magic: her servants hire pirates, rogues and thieves to prey on the roads and ports round the covenant (Ant p. 126).
stages.ignored: At the storyguide's choice she goes on with the raids and adds plague corpses in foreign dress, hidden in key places. From many lands, they carry many deadly diseases, which together wear down the people worse than she foresees; she may send help if too many die.
stages.stopped: She will be disappointed: magi need no Corpus magic to fight people. Beaten, the leader of a skilled, well-supplied band gives up a frame piece he swears is a great gold nugget; she has clouded his mind so he would not lose it.

stages.title: Herbam: Stolen Child
stages.clues: Set in a forest in hopes of interesting use of its wood. The Distinguished Herald takes a Gifted child, gives it to smoothfaces, then gossips among mortals that faeries have stolen a baby who could do some small wonder (any trick that shows the Gift), so that companions carry the tale home (Ant p. 127).
stages.ignored: The smoothfaces keep the child to draw faces for them.
stages.stopped: Return the baby and a frame piece is in its crib.
stages.turned: Enemies now, the smoothfaces may become allies at the end, if convinced the magi are strong and that the Queen's gift has endangered them.

stages.title: Ignem: The Ice Wyrm
stages.clues: Her servants catch an ice wyrm and move it by mirror to a quiet place near the covenant, and seven miles round it slowly freeze (Ant p. 127).
stages.ignored: The freeze forces the magi to go looking for it.
stages.stopped: Fire magic serves best against the wyrm and its weather. A frame piece lies in its little hoard of shiny things.

stages.title: Mentem: The Obvious Liar
stages.clues: An actor hired by her servant comes to the covenant as a merchant seeking his son, lost at a pilgrims' stop: blood in the bedding, and a lump of wood matted with gore and hair nearby. The real merchant is dead, killed by a Distinguished Servant, and little like him. The pilgrims recall no boy, but do recall a vanished merchant of that name (Ant pp. 127-128).
stages.ignored: Not caught quickly, the actor is spirited off to another kingdom by the Queen's Steward.
stages.stopped: Mentem magic sees through the act, questions the pilgrims, or speaks to the ghost of the merchant, buried by the road. The frame piece is a deodand at the nearest church, taken as the thing that beat a pilgrim to death: an object that has killed is sold, and the money goes to the family or stays with the church, as the clergy's honesty decides.

stages.title: Terram: We Did This Already!
stages.clues: The Herbam challenge over again, with knockers from a mine as her dupes. She cannot truly invent, and the repeat may show the magi that one hand is behind the stories (Ant p. 128).
stages.stopped: The knockers give up the child for oaths that it be rightly raised (p. 129).

stages.title: The Land of Gold and Glass
stages.clues: She wants the magi to come to terms with her, or even storm her kingdom; the frame is how (Ant pp. 128-129).
stages.ignored: A Faerie Magus? (p. 132): if she succeeds, her faerie magi serve as pawns in her later stories. Some faeries pose as magi already, and covenants must sometimes deal with them lest lords or the Church blame the Order, but hers cast, dress and speak with uncanny accuracy, and only a Code-breaking Intellego Vim gives them away.
stages.stopped:
Combat (pp. 129-131): her subjects rally to her, the Undistinguished Warriors and at the last the Distinguished Knight. Kill her and the princess can be freed. Take the bead's vis too, or she returns.

Too Boring (p. 131): magi who refuse the bait and stay in their laboratories are left alone; she wants no recluse for a servant. It is the least satisfying end and the easiest.

Too Powerful (p. 132): those able to raid her kingdom may use the frame; if they are very destructive she takes more care in provoking them.
stages.turned:
Too Clever (p. 131): she plays this game with other mortals too, and magi who keep interfering force her to terms.

Too Dangerous (p. 131): if her spies report that they can destroy strong faeries, the Distinguished Ambassador arranges a meeting and she offers a lasting peace, and asks their help to get objects of their replacements: it is easier for magi to walk through a target's Aegis. They must leave a common mirror in place of what they take, and she tells them how she took theirs.

Too Involved in Other Realms (pp. 131-132): those regularly aided by angels or demons are beyond her copying. She lets diabolists sink, with the frame pieces ordered away or into Deep Faerie, and keeps watch on the godly, whose piety may fail with time.

Too Interesting (p. 132): some truly epic work draws enough powerful faerie onlookers that she stops, so as not to disappoint them.

Too Useful (p. 132): magi who see through it can offer terms. A Merinita undergoing Becoming would be ideal, perhaps as the power behind her throne, or to redefine her role. More modestly, her minions serve and observe the magi as allies. She will not propose it herself, since models who know change the copy, but may be drawn by new kinds of human, or by objects of other magi whom they then challenge with her help.

neighbours.secrets:
The Queen's two goals: to run the magi through her stories, and to see Hermetic spells of every Form, so that her court wizards can imitate them (Ant p. 120). Roughly one story every four years. She is immortal; she knows mortals grow, so there is no sense in pressing them young; and any faster might sidetrack them, for she values spells against faeries less and does not want them over-specialized. Alter the frequency or count to suit the saga (p. 121).

Each story is tied to one Form, and tempts spells of it but forces none. She misreads Hermetic magic, so players who see the pattern can subvert it, which obliges her to step in herself. They are printed by Art and may come in any order, harder as the magi age. She sets no Vim story, being already a mistress of Vim and unwilling to give her minions weapons against spirits, and no Imaginem story, thinking it kin to glamour and missing its subtler uses. All are suggestions (p. 124).

If the magi do not play along (p. 125): burn the animals with fire and she simply adds another Animal story and wonders whether she still needs the Ignem one. She rarely knows when they have reached their limits. If the players tire of this, she either leaves them alone until they have other interests to exploit, or moves to the confrontation.

How the pattern shows (pp. 128-129): the frame pieces mark the link from the second piece on; she wants her hand known once she has her symbolic objects. Other victims, whom her servants introduce during The Obvious Liar, tell of repeated challenges that test growing skills. Questioning one (Communication + a fitting Ability, Ease Factor 15) brings back the event in which his symbolic object was taken, and the magi may then roll to recall theirs.

Intelligence + Faerie Lore on faeries and mirrors (p. 129): 12+ her title, and that her servants travel by mirror; 15+ they are reflections of real people, epitomes of human roles; 18+ some are shadows and reflections who spy; 21+ she has a kingdom in the faerie lands entered by mirrors. Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore (Ease Factor 15) finds the Bonisagus account.

neighbours.name: Breaking the Story
neighbours.summary: A strange place where a story seems to be waiting to happen: people say the same few lines over and over, walk fixed paths, and do not see that bits of the scenery are missing.
neighbours.secrets: Used as Arcane Connections to each other, the frame pieces can bring the magi to one of her stories before it is ready, to wreck it and enjoy a bizarre half-built setting. Played straighter, the setting is normal and the people unsure why they are there. To rule this out, keep the unfound pieces in Faerie, each let out only as its story begins (Ant p. 124).

neighbours.name: Firebrand Tytalus
neighbours.summary: A young Tytalus magus is at war with a local king, driving him and his people to their limits in the name of growth. It breaks the Code, and the Guernicus sent to look into it has been ambushed and shamed.
neighbours.secrets: The Tytalus is a duplicate. The Queen is designing a new steward, and uses this pawn to stretch the mortal who governs the kingdom (Ant p. 132).

neighbours.name: Blood of the Glass
neighbours.summary: A woman arrives to demand a baby bond, or the local equivalent, for a child she says one of the magi fathered. None of them knows anything about it.
neighbours.secrets: The child has very strong Faerie Blood of a new kind, and can make many kinds of imperishable Arcane Connection, as the Queen can. He is a source of guaranteed Insight for Original Research, and useful in Wizard's Marches. Do the magi let this be known? (Ant p. 132).

neighbours.name: The Malachite Caves
neighbours.summary: A dozen or so joined caverns in wild country far from anyone, by a river mouth or among sea caves. The rock shows fluted columns that glitter with shifting colors by torchlight, and the walls are banded with green malachite, with the odd emerald in roof and floor. Some linking passages are too narrow for a man; the others are worn glass-smooth and faintly rippled by the passing of serpents beyond number.

details.tethers: The labyrinthine caves (natural, 2); her long residence (preternatural, 2); the saga may add a waterfall (natural, 1), wave-carved stone (natural, 1) or a site of great rituals (preternatural, 1-2).

levels.name: The Malachite Mound
levels.see: The floor is one great mound of solid malachite, with a deep spiral groove cut around it.
levels.enter: Ease Factor 11 for the fitting Supernatural Ability (ArM5 p. 189), from the deepest cavern.
levels.notes: Walking the spiral to the summit, at the middle of the room, passes through a gate into the Magic Realm.

neighbours.secrets:
The saga chooses where the caves lie, but they must be near water and in a Magic aura of at least 5, with some local feature to explain it, by tethers added together (Realms of Power: Magic p. 8). The aura is 3 by the entrance and rises with depth to 8 in the last cave, reached by no direct way though its passages are the widest, ten feet across on average. (pp. 138-139)

Each cave holds serpents of mixed sizes, who resent intruders but hardly talk to each other, so a party meets one caveful at a time. On the first visit their mother is away. A lone serpent two years older than any yet met will seem the mistress of them all; for a harder fight, a horde attacks as an untrained group. Killing them does not stop the thefts. (pp. 138-139)

Area spells catch several at once. An Individual of Ignem fills the volume of one Size 0 creature, which is two of Size -1, five of Size -2, ten of Size -3 or twenty of Size -4, and so on. A Pilum of Fire can hit two hundred hatchlings, or fifty with five yearlings and a two-year-old. Once alert they spread out, cutting such spells to between a half and a third. Sealed in, they simply wait. (p. 138)

neighbours.name: The Waimie's Insula
neighbours.summary: A cave like those of the world outside but immeasurably larger, floored with hundreds of malachite mounds from a few feet across to the size of hills, each scored with a spiral. The spirals run both ways and interlock, and from a height they look like a map or a foreign, curling script. The land changes, too slowly to watch, as if a nest of snakes were languidly coiling.
neighbours.secrets:
Enclosed by an Animal Boundary of level 4: the effective Magic aura is 14, or 18 for anything to do with Animal, her Magic Resistance and Penetration among them. Any magical activity has four extra botch dice. (p. 140)

Even with her dead a child may hide here and grow to be a new danger, and visitors from elsewhere in the Magic Realm, serpents and dragons most of all, slip through the boundary. The storyguide peoples its far reaches. (p. 140)

Crossing a boundary has a base Ease Factor of 18, ignoring Familiarity; using a vestige has (10 - vestige level) x 3. See Realms of Power: Magic p. 23. (p. 141)

neighbours.name: The Serpent Map
neighbours.summary: The landscape of the insula itself, read by moving across it.
neighbours.secrets:
Both a map and a book in the speech of serpents: an intelligent snake crossing it begins to take in a chart of part of the Magic Realm, marked with its marvels and dangers. (pp. 140-141)

A season's study is a Summa on Area Lore: Magic Realm, Level 5, Quality 4. With the Animal Ken Virtue the Quality is the Animal Ken score if over 5; a Bjornaer with a snake heartbeast uses an effective Language score of 5 (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p. 23); and spending half the season as a serpent adds 3. (p. 141)

At the storyguide's option it can locate things, at a week's study per 3 points of Ease Factor and a roll of Intelligence + Area Lore: Magic Realm: a Magic aura at 9 + aura, a Magic regio at 12 + its highest aura, a vis source at 15 + its yearly pawns, a Magic Realm gate at 18. Success lets the reader trace the place from any known aura in the mundane world. (p. 141)

neighbours.name: The Marjoram Grove
neighbours.summary: A far-off grove where marjoram grows.
neighbours.secrets: The Waimie's own vis source, which feeds her Hunger for Animal Magic and which she prizes above all other vis. Each year a child of hers gathers three sprigs as the star Regulus rises; the herb stills the carrier's venom for the trip home. The book gives no pawn count and no place. (p. 136)

neighbours.name: The Church's Parcel in the Valley
neighbours.summary: The one parcel in the valley where cows ever gave good milk; elsewhere it came out foul and acrid. The freeman who held it died childless and left it to the Church, which lets it to local serfs for garden crops.
neighbours.secrets: Those who know her appetite may guess why she liked the milk: put back to pasture, the land would give cows whose milk yields Creo vis. The book gives no amount. (p. 138)

neighbours.name: The Stream of the Insula
neighbours.summary: A stream crossing one part of the insula.
neighbours.secrets: A boundary into an insula aligned to Aquam. A sample exit: the storyguide sets the true destination. (p. 141)

neighbours.name: The Great Ivy Root
neighbours.summary: The root of a huge ivy against one wall, climbing out of sight.
neighbours.secrets: A climber crosses this Herbam boundary into an insula ruled by plants. A sample exit: the storyguide sets the true destination. (p. 141)

neighbours.name: The Malachite Statue
neighbours.summary: A little abstract statue of the same malachite on a small mound, all arches and rings, which from some angles suggests a dancing woman.
neighbours.secrets: A Terram vestige of level 4, of a Mystery Cult of dancers who raise fertility by their art. It is present too in an insula of Mentem and one of Corpus. A sample exit: the storyguide sets the true destination. (p. 141)

neighbours.name: The Phantom Mouse
neighbours.summary: A mouse that runs through the lair, glimpsed from the corner of the eye or heard as tiny feet.
neighbours.secrets: An Imaginem vestige of level 2, tied to the dream of a cat that is a magus' familiar. It appears in several insulae, and whoever catches it can travel with it to them. A sample exit: the storyguide sets the true destination. (p. 141)

neighbours.name: The Cult of the Serpent
neighbours.summary: A band of folk who speak of a Scaly Queen and go about gathering news.
neighbours.secrets: An option for a stronger Waimie, not part of the story as printed. They gather information and vis for her. Her human servants are perhaps held by a power like the Entrancement Ability. (p. 136)

neighbours.name: The Stolen Vis
neighbours.summary: Someone has been at the covenant's vis before the magi could get there. A snake has been seen near the place.

stages.title: The Empty Vis Source
stages.clues: A portable vis source, gathered without magic or skill, is found already stripped, and again the next year. Anyone left on guard sees a yearling snake come for it, knowing just where the vis is and how to take it.
stages.ignored: She has a share of the covenant's vis every year.
stages.stopped: The thief's fate depends on the guards. (p. 136)

stages.title: A Bigger Thief Each Year
stages.clues: If the yearling was opposed, a two-year-old comes next year, perhaps the same snake, scarred, perhaps not. Each year a bigger one comes until one gets away with the vis; then that size until it keeps failing.
stages.ignored: She wants vis home at least every other year on average, and sends whatever size will do it.
stages.turned: The corpses hold Animal vis, so the covenant may treat this as a contested source. She answers by sending a tiny serpent with each large one, to fetch the dead sibling's eyes. (p. 136)

stages.title: The Theft Spreads
stages.clues: After some years a hatchling lurks near the covenant, unseen, and trails anyone who leaves, hoping to be led to more vis. On the third source the magi may notice: one snake too many.
stages.ignored: She begins robbing a second source; with no other suitable source she gets nothing. (pp. 136-137)

stages.title: The Covenant Raided
stages.clues: While the spotted hatchling is chased, a serpent one year older than any yet met enters the covenant, seeking vis by Magic Sensitivity at Ease Factor 12 less the pawns present.
stages.ignored: With a single store she may eat three-quarters of it before being found; with vis in each sanctum, she reaches two or three. Found, she flees for home to bring it all up for her mother, unless the opposition is slight, when she may stay and kill grogs.
stages.stopped: A strong Aegis may hold her out, so the fight is outside the walls. Traps in stores or sancta can stop her. (p. 137)

stages.title: Investigations
stages.clues: The locals have tales, contradictory ones, on the way to or from the cave. A serpent can be followed home: the smaller, the harder. They shun settled land and keep to rivers and the sea, and unless the trackers draw notice they are not seen. (pp. 137-138)

stages.title: The Lair
stages.clues: The caves teem with serpents, but the mother is in her absent season.
stages.ignored: Fighting her children changes nothing: she breeds more, and larger ones are with her in the Magic Realm.
stages.stopped: Best shown as a meeting with bigger serpents than yet seen, still low in the order, to set up the next stage. (p. 138)

stages.title: Besieged
stages.clues: Having lost too much to the magi, she wants revenge and sends a daughter of at least eight years against a place they value: the covenant, a vis site, even a village. Swollen by Scion of the World Serpent to as much as Size +12 and 265 feet, she rings it, enclosing up to 70 feet across, in overlapping coils if it is smaller, with her head at the main gate; or she lies along the edge of an Aegis that stops her.
stages.ignored: She stays until killed or driven off. Outward-opening doors are jammed; anyone going in or out is attacked; supplies are swallowed or flung far away.
stages.stopped: Parma may turn her attacks, for her Penetration with this power is Might + aura modifier, but she can still swallow a magus, harmless as that is if horrid. A stealthy character may slip by her poor eyes, though her Magic Sensitivity hinders invisibility. Magi who see her size flicker at dawn or dusk may break her attention then, so she cannot renew the power. (p. 139)

stages.title: Final Showdown
stages.clues: Following her children back, through the deepest cave and the regio, the magi climb the spiral to her lair in the Magic Realm.
stages.stopped: She is extremely hard to kill at home; the characters may need another answer than a straight fight. (pp. 139-140)
stages.turned: She will take a tithe of vis in place of the thefts. (p. 141)

links.note: The first thief at the vis source

neighbours.secrets:
A serpent of the Magic Realm is sending her young to rob the covenant's vis, first at its sources, then at home. She suits a run of linked stories close together better than a saga-long theme, and her brood start small and grow more dangerous. (pp. 7, 133)

She need not be killed: she will settle for a tithe of vis, smaller perhaps than what her children would steal, with no lives lost. (p. 141)

neighbours.name: The Queen's Vis
neighbours.summary: A small serpent leaves the lair on some errand of its own, each year at the same time.
neighbours.secrets: Whoever watches the lair and follows her can reach the marjoram. Taking it from her gives a strong hand with the Waimie, who may hold off the thefts for as long as he has it hostage. (p. 136)

neighbours.name: The Rebellious Daughter
neighbours.summary: One of the great serpents does not attack on sight.
neighbours.secrets: See the daughter's record. If the characters meet her needs she will stand with them against her mother; whether she can be trusted after that remains to be seen. (p. 136)

neighbours.name: Wrong Side of the Fence
neighbours.summary: The siege finds the covenant's people on both sides of the serpent.
neighbours.secrets: Those outside learn that what they need against her (vis, a ritual's casting tablet, an enchantment) is inside, and must get it past the coils. (p. 139)

neighbours.name: Not Alone
neighbours.summary: A redcap brings word that a Hermetic rival is losing vis to the same thieves, and proposes a summit.
neighbours.secrets: The rival wants the meeting held at the players' covenant. Some suspect a motive beyond the alliance against her; surely not? (p. 139)

neighbours.name: The Serpent's Husband
neighbours.summary: A friendly man is met walking in the Waimie's lair.
neighbours.secrets: See his record: is he all he seems? (p. 140)

neighbours.name: Have We Made Things Worse?
neighbours.summary: The great serpent is dead, and serpents are still seen.
neighbours.secrets: Her death frees the brood. The young wander lost, and stay until Acclimation makes them plain serpents or their elders eat them. The older flee to find auras and vis sources of their own; some may mature to her statistics and, with mates, brood. With enough auras about there may be several Waimies competing for one set of vis sources, or a war until one rules. (p. 141)

neighbours.name: Unwelcome Visitors
neighbours.summary: Strangers from the Magic Realm begin to ask after the serpent's lair.
neighbours.secrets: A few beings of the Magic Realm know of the Serpent Map and will not leave the characters to it. Some are only chancers, but what it holds is of use to mighty beings, and one will come in time, perhaps far worse than she was. (p. 141)

characters.name: Bishop Orris

description.biography:
Equipment: ruby ring of office, clerical vestments. He may also carry the Hand of St. John, particularly if he fears for his life from supernatural sources; he does not routinely carry the cathedral's relics when he enters the saga. Encumbrance 0 (0).

As printed (p. 51): Faith Score 0 (1), the point coming from taking the Eucharist. Dodge: Init -1, Attack n/a, Defense -1, Damage n/a. Soak -1. Fatigue levels OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wound penalties -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

The block gives Magic Sensitivity as 3+2, the +2 from Puissant, Organization Lore: Order of Hermes as 0 (2), and Divine Lore and Civil & Canon Lore, entered here as Dominion Lore and Civil and Canon Law. Meddler is taken as the Major Flaw, by its place in the block's list.

Both his Supernatural Abilities are Divine: no supernatural aura penalizes them, and a Dominion aura adds to them (p. 51).

characters.summary:
The bishop of the diocese, a long, gaunt man with a great beak of a nose and bright blue eyes. The red hair of his youth has gone white, though he has kept it all but the tonsure. In the pulpit he is formidable, with a big voice and a sure command of argument, and he can move a congregation.

He is a local man made good, the second son of a wealthy knight who grew up in the diocese and served as a parish priest in it before his election, and the city is proud of him. He preaches in his people's own tongue, unlike the standoffish bishop before him, and knows their troubles. He is known for his sense of justice, for mediating disputes between prominent locals, and for standing with the poor against the powerful. The citizens love to see him face down lords who lean on the free men of the city.

Churchmen think well of him. The story goes that a saint called him to religion in a dream. He joined the Benedictines, then after ordination won release from his monastic vows to take a parish, against his family's wishes. The abbey where he was a novice was abandoned soon after, for innocent reasons. He was known for quiet faith, strength of character and efficiency, and his election surprised no one.
characters.secrets:
He senses evil and the good in people's hearts, and he senses magic, but his curse makes the two one to him. He has met the power of Hell and feels the same thing around magic, and has never felt magic any other way, so he does not know the two can be told apart. Add his piety and his dread of the Infernal, and he takes the characters for Hell's allies (pp. 50, 57). He is a good man acting for his flock: run him as a puzzle to solve, not a monster to beat (p. 50).

Who cursed him is the storyguide's choice (p. 57). God or an angel, to test whether the characters will keep the high ground and hold back their power. A demon, years ago, when he was a rising priest, so that a dangerous enemy of Hell would waste himself on magic and the innocent. Or a powerful hedge wizard or faerie he offended when young: fittingly, he probably saw something he did not understand and called it the Devil's work.

What he knows of the Order (pp. 52-53): a working knowledge, partly wrong through the Order's own misinformation (Lords of Men pp. 40-41). He thinks covenants are like chapters or monasteries; he knows, unless they have hidden it, that this one lies in his diocese, and perhaps its name. He has never met a magus and expects blue robes, tall brimmed blue hats and staves. He knows of the Order's laws, its secret Tribunals and its democracy. Sorcerers he has met seemed evil to him. He accepts in reason that not all wizards are evil, but God has given him the power to know evil, and he reserves judgment until he meets them himself.

His Magic Sensitivity (p. 56): near a Divine, Infernal or Magic manifestation he grows dizzy and breaks into a cold sweat. The Divine brings joy and rays of golden light from the source; Infernal or Magic things are hard to look at, wrapped in gloom and hollow despair. He must Penetrate any Magic Resistance to feel anything. The Ease Factor to detect a Gifted person is 15 minus the highest Art divided by 5, or the highest Supernatural Ability. Next to the altar his Dominion aura of 5 and the Just temper add to the roll. A character on trial stands in aura 5, bystanders in aura 4; subtract 3 times the aura from Magic Resistance within the Dominion. He may detect a spell or an enchanted item instead. If he fails to Penetrate, the target feels something rebuffed. The storyguide may simply rule that he succeeds.

What a character knows of him (p. 54): Intelligence + Organization Lore: Church, or a stress die + his Reputation of 4 without it; everything up to the highest Ease Factor beaten. Botch: facts about a different bishop. 3: this is Bishop Orris. 6: he is thought fair, and his city is proud of him. 9: he is a local, raised about ten miles from here. 12: he is influential in his city and a powerful orator. 15: he has been very hard on sorcerers.

Holy Influence (pp. 55, 57): Presence + Leadership + stress die. 9 grants +1, 15 grants +2, 24 grants +3. The temper of the Dominion is described in RoP: The Divine Revised Edition pp. 38-40.

His frame of mind (p. 62): he spends night after night prostrate on the chancel steps, praying for a sign that he judges rightly and that his way is the only way to protect his people. A spy in the cathedral may learn from this that he is no villain and that peace can still be found.

Attacking him (p. 66): he may be warned of a plot in a dream, and if the characters are thought ruthless he may hire bodyguards and keep the relics by him. The Hand gives Magic Resistance 40, and his usual Dominion aura of at least 4 raises it to 44. He prays for a miracle if attacked. Beyond that he is an aging man who has never fought and is easily killed.

Reworking him (pp. 53-54). Not a bishop: an abbot changes least; a Templar preceptor or a pious noble tied to the clergy, perhaps by a younger brother, may need rebuilt, more martial statistics. Other motives: he may not be deluded at all, but resent the magi's power or covet a resource such as an income. Then the Cantores help him less, Theodoric may side with the characters, and his allies are less loyal. He could be truly corrupt, but use this with care: it is a tired figure, it loses the dilemma, and angels and saints make such a man unlikely in that seat.

More powerful (pp. 53-54): an archbishop or cardinal has personal Magic Resistance that stacks with relics, and the Commanding Aura (RoP: The Divine Revised Edition pp. 42-43; The Church p. 26). An archbishop's cathedral should have another 500 Build Points. The Cantores may gain Holy Powers and act at his direction; Understanding would give him counsel and visions of what the characters do. A Templar, Hospitaller or Teutonic preceptory in his city brings the knights in sooner, their engines protected by a Cantores Blessing of Magic Resistance. Weaker: he is a busy man and can afford to move slowly unless they retaliate, so make him less ardent.

characters.name: Archdeacon Geoffrey
characters.summary: The senior archdeacon of the diocese and the only one ordained a priest, so he is also called Father Geoffrey. He is at home in the intrigues of the bishop's household and likes to think of himself as the power behind the throne.
characters.secrets:
He is nothing of the kind: Orris has seen his ambition and keeps real influence out of his hands (p. 51). He loves money and skims diocesan funds when he thinks it safe.

He found Turstan, the bishop's double, a few years ago, and takes fees from clients for having the "bishop" bless new premises and ventures (p. 63). The summoner of the visitation may be in league with him, inventing sins for the fees and fines (p. 54).

The covenant lies in his archdeaconry. Orris questions him about it and has him ask around at his next visitation (p. 58).

characters.name: Deacon Adam
characters.summary: The bishop's devoted secretary, who is also chamberlain and steward of his household and his manservant. He guards his place at the bishop's side so jealously that he lets no one share the work, and goes about overworked and nearly always exhausted.

characters.name: Father Peter
characters.summary: The provost of St. John's canons, and the bishop's confessor and confidant. He is old, suspects he has little time left, and worries that no one can follow him. He respects Brother Theodoric as a true mystic, but does not count him fit for so worldly a task.
characters.secrets:
He could sway the bishop a great deal and has never tried (p. 51). He knows the bishop better than anyone, so an angel or saint guiding the characters might turn them toward him (p. 63). He works hard to soothe the canons who feel passed over by the Cantores (p. 52).

Theology 5, as the cathedral's provost of canons (p. 52).

characters.name: Brother Theodoric
characters.summary: The chief chorister of St. John's and its most experienced singer. He is no natural leader, and does not notice that some canons feel snubbed.
characters.secrets:
