The de facto head of the Holy Tradition of Cantores, which he founded here ten years ago. He picks recruits by the visions he receives. He has True Faith (p. 52), and Holy Music 8 as chief chorister (p. 52).

If Orris's motives are made selfish, Theodoric may turn ally to the characters (p. 53). If the bishop is murdered, his ghost may come to Theodoric and tell how he died (p. 66).

characters.name: Baron Geoffroi d'Arques

params.detail: Learn all there is about the supernatural

description.physical_description: Clean-shaven, upright and well turned out, with the best of everything about him, from armor and travelling clothes to the gold rings on his fingers, and a horse, saddle and barding to match.
description.biography:
As printed at the start of his story, just as the fascination takes him (Ant p. 9). The book prints no later block: his scores change little, except that his knowledge of the realms grows.

Combat, with superior arms and armor counted: Dodge Init -2, Defense +2. Fist Init -2, Attack +5, Defense +3, Damage +1. Lance and heater shield (mounted) Init +0, Attack +14, Defense +12, Damage +6. Long sword and heater shield Init +0, Attack +12, Defense +11, Damage +7. Long sword and heater shield (mounted) Init +0, Attack +15, Defense +14, Damage +7. Great sword Init +0, Attack +13, Defense +8, Damage +10. Soak +11. Encumbrance 3 (4).

Fatigue levels: OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wound penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Equipment: superior full chain armor (+1 soak), superior long sword (+1 attack), superior heater shield (+1 defense), a great sword, and a horse for every occasion.

Advancement (Ant p. 9): Wealthy gives him three free seasons, for 20 experience points a year: two seasons taught at quality 7, 14 points in one or two Abilities; a season's practice at quality 4 in a martial Ability; and a season's exposure, 2 points in a language or Order of Hermes Lore. Once his Latin is better he takes tuition in the four realm lores as tutors can be found.

Optional rule (Ant p. 9): a troupe may give him Ability Block (Supernatural), balanced by Temporal Influence. The book offers this as a choice and does not list either in his block.

characters.summary: A wealthy Norman nobleman of thirty-two, baron of Arques and lately come to look after some distant manors he had long ignored. He is a superb soldier, known on the French tourney circuit, and astute enough to know that he is no great politician. He is married with several children, one of them an acknowledged bastard, has few enemies, and has always been a God-fearing man who takes faeries and unicorns for tales.
characters.secrets:
His first brush with the supernatural turns into an obsession. He wants it for three reasons: plain curiosity, in an idle and secure lord; display, since a noble who commands an enchanter outshines one who pays a painter, and can give magical prizes and gifts and keep a veiled threat over his rivals; and use, with crops, spies and victories to be had from the right magician (Ant p. 13).

He can never learn a Supernatural Ability himself. He attempts Initiations, but he is too much the master of his domain to be anyone's apprentice, so they all fail, and he contents himself with keeping those who have the gifts he lacks (Ant p. 9). Every time he reappears after the first meeting he should have some new magical possession to show off (Ant p. 10).

He suspects, but cannot be sure, that François is his son, and may have an astrologer settle it (Ant pp. 10, 21).

Relocating him (Ant pp. 8-10): he is a lesser baron and need not stay one. He needs enough wealth to spend his time on this, secure lands, and holdings both near the covenant and far enough off to explain long absences. In a saga set near Arques, move his old lands elsewhere. The local manors may be a dowry, an inheritance, or won by conquest or at a tourney.

characters.name: Ysabeau

description.physical_description: An attractive young woman, always elegantly dressed, and fond of a golden necklace her husband gave her not long ago.
description.biography:
Stat block: Ant p. 11. A minor supporting character, with few Virtues and Flaws; the book invites a troupe to add to her.

Combat: Dodge Init -1, Defense -1. Fist Init -1, Attack +2, Defense -1, Damage -1. Soak -1. Encumbrance 0 (0).

Fatigue levels: OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wound penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Equipment: an elegant gown and a superior gold necklace, which adds +1 to first-impression Charm rolls: her Charm is printed 5 + 1.

characters.summary: The baron's wife and the mother of his three legitimate children, a young woman of twenty-five. She runs her household with assurance and is modest and quiet before her husband and his guests.
characters.secrets:
Her first care is the safety and future of her children. She loves Geoffroi, but as his obsession grows she can be brought to put them before him, which makes her the weak link the characters can work on (Ant pp. 10, 11). She knows of Guillaume and does not know of François.

Near the end she fears for her children, for his people, and that his lands will fall to his wizards or to knights picking over his failing estates. She can tell the covenant what is planned for Alenard, who is to take him, and that for all his Initiations Geoffroi has never learned the least piece of magic (Ant p. 19).

characters.name: Claude de Fécamp

description.physical_description: A slight man, neither tall nor short, bald by the razor, with a long and sober face. His right arm stops at the elbow, and he keeps the empty sleeve of his habit pinned up.
description.biography:
Stat block: Ant p. 12.

Combat: Dodge Init -4, Defense -4. Soak +1, or +6 with the +5 his guardian angel grants. Encumbrance 0 (0).

Fatigue levels: OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wound penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Divine Resistance 15: the angel gives him Magic Resistance +15 aligned with the Divine while he acts in accord with God's will.

Equipment: a plain monk-style habit, a wooden crucifix, and a purse usually holding enough for most expenses.

characters.summary: The baron's steward, twenty-eight, trusted with much of his business and met as often as the baron himself. Schooled at a Benedictine monastery, he has served the household for six years and is known for his loyalty and sobriety.
characters.secrets:
In his first year he resented his master's wealth and his own place, and made enemies. One night persons unknown beat him almost to death, and an angel enfolded him and showed him his faults. He renewed his loyalty and gave up his old ways, and the angel promised him protection while he stays true. The household barely remembers the man he was (Ant p. 12).

He is loyal to the end and cannot be turned by mundane means (Ant p. 10).

characters.name: Guillaume
characters.summary: The baron's eldest son, twelve, a bastard by a woman of low birth, openly acknowledged. He is getting his education on the Normandy tourney circuit.
characters.secrets: Geoffroi means to give him much of his land as an appanage, held until Guillaume's death. If the baron is left to decline, Guillaume is among those fighting over the estates (Ant pp. 19, 20).

characters.name: François
characters.summary: A boy of ten, brought up as the son of a man of rank in Normandy.
characters.secrets: He is the baron's bastard by a married woman of rank, though only she and Geoffroi suspect it and neither can be sure, and the boy knows nothing. Her resentment of Geoffroi has kept his Loyalty at 0. Made public, it would set a vengeful cuckold on the baron's Norman lands (Ant pp. 10, 20).

characters.name: Alenard
characters.summary: The baron's son and heir, seven years old and as demanding a young prince as any.
characters.secrets: His Loyalty may change as he grows and understands where he stands beside his brothers. Geoffroi means him for magic, and promises him to one of the court's wizards (Ant pp. 10, 16, 19). He comes to resent how his father has used him.

characters.name: Joie
characters.summary: The baron's elder legitimate daughter, five years old.

characters.name: Viollette
characters.summary: The baron's younger legitimate daughter, three years old.

characters.name: Edwin Locke

description.physical_description: A man well into middle age with thinning gray hair, confident and determined in his bearing.
description.biography:
Stat block: Ant p. 16. An unGifted Mythic Companion, who may take four more Virtues balanced by two further Flaws. The book prints his Arts as (Theurgical) Controlling 15 +3 and (Theurgical) Summoning 15, and the four Elementalist Forms as Difficult Arts.

Combat: Dodge Init +0, Defense +0. Fist Init +0, Attack +0, Defense +0, Damage +0. Bludgeon Init -1, Attack +2, Defense +0, Damage +2. Soak +2. Encumbrance 0 (0).

Fatigue levels: OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wound penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Equipment: philosophical texts and an astrolabe.

Vis: 4 pawns each of Aquam, Auram, Ignem and Terram, as glass-like crystals in small bottles of preservative oil, in a wooden case made for them.

reputations.name: Tutor at York Cathedral School (among academics)

characters.summary: An academic from the north of England and a prominent tutor at York's cathedral school, forty years old, with the look of a man left permanently unamused by his students.
characters.secrets: An elementalist, unGifted. He neither hides his magic from his colleagues nor discusses it, and lives two lives, one in the cathedral and one among spirits and supernatural beasts. He knows little of the realms themselves, but knows of other traditions and of the Order, and sees meeting them as an intellectual challenge (Ant p. 16). He is the likeliest of the wizards to go out and bring others to the court (Ant p. 12), and may take Claude's place as steward (Ant p. 18).

characters.name: Walter de Gray
characters.summary: The patron and adviser of Edwin Locke of York.

characters.name: Ádhamh Brathair
characters.summary: A learned scholar from Hibernia at the baron's court. His name is said EWE BRO-hur.
characters.secrets: A learned magician, who means to build one unified theory of magic on sound philosophy. He studies his colleagues' magic and pursues the breakthroughs the theory needs.

characters.name: Dominici Viterbo
characters.summary: A scholar who has lately joined the baron's court.
characters.secrets: A goetic sorcerer, desperate to escape a dark fate, who hopes to hide in the council. The demons of his past soon find him. By teaching others he may mend his mistakes and cleanse his arts of their corruption.

characters.name: Hannelore of the Baron's Council
characters.summary: A woman who has joined the baron's council of scholars.
characters.secrets: A student of the Maleficia who brings Infernal magic to the council for protection from Hermetic enemies of her past. She wants a direct road to influence, and sets out to take Ysabeau's place in the baron's affections.

characters.name: Jabir Al-Qazwini
characters.summary: An Arabic magus who has travelled far to the baron's court.
characters.secrets: An itinerant sahir, seeking a council of the wise that a powerful spirit of the sands promised him. He believes he has found it and stays to learn, seemingly blind to the baron's decline and the council's growing power.

characters.name: Carles Peregrinus
characters.summary: A man with a grievance, newly welcome at the baron's council.
characters.secrets: A failed Hermetic apprentice, denied what he sees as his place in the Order. He means to dominate the council through his strong Entrancement.

characters.name: Baron Giraud Le Cornu

description.biography:
Combat (Ant p. 25). Lance and Heater, mounted: Init 0, Attack +16, Defense +14, Damage +6. Long sword and Heater, mounted: Init 0, Attack +14, Defense +13, Damage +7. Long sword and Heater, dismounted: Init 0, Attack +11, Defense +10, Damage +7. Long sword, dismounted: Init 0, Attack +11, Defense +7, Damage +7. Soak +11. Fatigue Levels: OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wound Penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+). Encumbrance 3 (4).

Equipment: warhorse (courser), full chain mail, heater shield, lance, long sword, a diary, and several relics.

Tall and fair, clean shaven, his hair cropped to sit under a helmet, with a keen and measuring look. His clothes are good and a little old-fashioned. He weighs his words, and speaks like a man used to being obeyed.

He holds Hatred (Major) against rebels. The block prints Intrigue and Ride as 4 (5), so each has 5 xp beyond its score. In England, take Common Law in place of Civil and Canon Law (Ant p. 25). He has no supernatural powers and no Magic Resistance (Ant p. 27). If the magi are at odds with him for some years, his habits earn him a local Reputation as Eccentric, at a score the book does not print (Ant p. 30).

The name is Norman French and may be changed to suit the saga; his overlord is a count here, but takes whatever title suits the covenant's lands, and should not be a king or emperor (Ant p. 25). Lords of Men pp. 30-36 lists titles by region.

characters.summary:
A young baron and a rising man at his count's court, praised for loyalty, courage, courtesy, initiative and a shrewd head, and known among his peers as learned, a good negotiator and resourceful in battle. He rides out eagerly against anyone who defies the count.

All the region knows how he came by his lands: when his father rose against the count, Giraud pretended to stand with him and then delivered him up. Some call that a ruthless grab for favor, others a knight's duty to his liege over his kin.
characters.secrets:
He does not want the covenant's land or wealth, nor even its allegiance to himself. He wants the magi to be law-abiding as he understands it, which means sworn to some mundane lord, and so in breach of the Code of Hermes. In his view anyone who owes fealty to no one is a king, the Pope or a rebel (Ant pp. 26-27).

The more he learns of magic, the more he fears it: magi could seize his liege's mind or appear at his bedside with a knife. Unless they are bound into the web of allegiance that holds nobles in check, they threaten him, his family and his lord (Ant p. 27; Lords of Men pp. 42-43 says why the feudal order survives them).

He expects to be bewitched or killed, so his wife, his confessor and his brother know all his plans and any of them could take up the campaign. His sons join that circle when they reach 21 (Ant p. 29).

He would balk at a pact with demons, but only if he knew them for what they were (Ant p. 30).

characters.name: Lady Éloise Le Cornu
characters.summary: The baron's wife, a capable manager who runs the barony in his long absences at court or at war. She sits in most of his councils and negotiations. She decides quickly, seldom thinks again, and does not take advice.
characters.secrets:
She is unsure of herself in her duties and hides it behind a show of authority. Facing the magi while he is away, she starts out harder and less patient than he is (Ant pp. 25-26).

She knows all his plans, and is his likeliest choice to run his network of agents (Ant p. 29). With her or his confessor he arranges secret meetings with the covenant's malcontents (Ant p. 29).

If the saga runs for several years she grows used to authority: she loses Headstrong and gains Innovative +1 (Ant p. 26).

characters.name: Brother Henri Raoullin
characters.summary: The baron's chaplain, confessor, clerk and legal adviser, with some training in the law. He picks his words with care and always has the right proverb from Scripture. He steadies his lord, and he may come to the covenant under a white flag to ease a quarrel.
characters.secrets: He willingly helps with the baron's intrigues, and knows all his plans. He wants to learn all he can of the magi: first that they are neither diabolists nor heretics, then that they do not ill-use Christians. His hand shows in any terms the baron offers, and he judges whether the magi have satisfied the baron that their powers are not Infernal (Ant pp. 26, 29, 35).

characters.name: Sir Artur Le Cornu
characters.summary: The baron's younger brother and one of his vassal knights, much his brother's kind: the stronger man, but the slower. He cannot read or write and has less intrigue and courtly grace, yet he is less ruled by his passions. He would rule as steward if the baron died before his heir came of age.
characters.secrets:
He has come to accept the betrayal of their father as right for the realm, but doubts he could have done it himself. He knows all his brother's plans (Ant pp. 26, 29).

If he takes over the barony he soon learns intrigue and becomes nearly as dangerous. He is readier than his brother to hire hedge wizards against the magi and less willing to heed Brother Raoullin (Ant p. 26).

characters.name: Bertrand Gallain
characters.summary: One of the baron's two household squires and his herald, better fitted for diplomacy than for battle, though he hopes for knighthood. A younger son of a poor knight, he dresses finely and judges everyone at first sight, as he expects to be judged.
characters.secrets:
He puts on airs to hide his humble start. He is loyal at bottom, but his taste for luxury and rank leaves him open to bribes and flattery (Ant p. 26).

A magus without the Gentle Gift who meets him is reported to the baron as a wicked, untrustworthy sort (Ant p. 27).

characters.name: Father Joseph of Napoli

description.biography:
Combat (Ant p. 38). Dodge: Init -1, Attack +1, Defense -1, Damage n/a. Soak +2 (-1 Stamina, +3 papal legate). Fatigue Levels: OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wound Penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+). Encumbrance 0.

Magic Resistance 25: 15 as a papal legate and 10 from his relic. Faith Points 2: 1 from the relic, which regenerates, and 1 from mass. Age 54, looking 44, with a Longevity Ritual of +5. Powers: Commanding Aura as papal legate, and Faithful Wisdom from the relic. Arthritis and Visions are due to Warping, and his Ability Block is Martial.

Equipment: priest's stole, a well-worn monk's habit, the finger-bone relic, letters of authority in a leather scroll case, writing gear (ink, parchment, the legate's seal, wax and so on), and a riding horse with saddle and tack.

Tall and ascetic, with a slight stoop from years at the writing desk, though he straightens and his eyes shine when he preaches. He is plainly old but not frail. He wears a priest's regalia, carries a satchel of writing gear, and rides a black stallion worth a great deal, built for speed and able to go for days with little rest. One or two clergymen ride with him, and later perhaps a magus ally dressed as one.

Commanding Aura (Ant p. 38; DE p. 82, same figures): as Aura of Rightful Authority at Voice Range, at no cost and with no Penetration, with Magic Resistance 15 and Soak +3, the Magic Resistance added to any relic's. It fails if he delays or strays from his mission, until he does penance, and ends when the mission is done. It comes from his office, not his letters (Ant p. 43).

He has no True Faith and cannot work miracles, though he can pray to the saints (Ant p. 39). His Magic Resistance does not stop him crossing an Aegis of the Hearth, but the relic's Divine Might needs a token there, unless the Aegis is too weak to stop it; he can leave it behind (Ant p. 41). Replace his Area Lores and Living Languages if his past is moved to another Tribunal (Ant p. 40). A storyguide rolls Order of Hermes Lore, Code of Hermes, Magic Theory or Area Lore for anything rare he might know (Ant p. 40).

reputations.name: Papal Legate to the Order of Hermes (ecclesiastical)

characters.summary:
A papal legate sent as envoy to the Order of Hermes, who introduces himself as such and hides nothing of his past. A fisherman's son of Napoli, he left the Church as a deacon at 19 to serve as notary to the Quaesitor Pompius, and traveled with him through the Rome and Rhine Tribunals for almost 17 years. After Pompius passed into Final Twilight in 1202 he went home, became a canon at San Giovanni Maggiore and wrote about the Order. Ordained in 1210 and soon called to Rome to advise Innocent III on the Order, he stayed on under Honorius III, who made him legate in 1219.

He is a good man who tries to live by Christ's teaching, a patient talker rather than a fighter, and no saint. He proposes that the Order become a true religious order under a Grand Master and the pope, and he wants magi to think and talk about it.
characters.secrets:
His mission has three parts: seat a Grand Master, have him recognized by the pope as a Christian title, subject to Rome, and in time have anyone who refuses the new Order Marched. He expects that to mean devout pagans, Muslims and Jews who will not convert, and those who want to stay free of Rome. Wizard War waged by his allies would also serve, but he prefers a March's legal clarity (Ant p. 37).

He has no quarrel with magic. Canon law would stretch to cover magi as a new order of religious, with the Code and the Peripheral Codes as new volumes of it. Houses, Tribunals, independence and scholarship may all stay, and arcane theories would be treated as Church theologians' are: some embraced, some tolerated, a few outlawed (Ant pp. 37-38).

He still knows many covenants of Rome and Rhine, some hidden in regiones, their sites and numbers nearly twenty years stale, and little of magi Gauntleted since. He knows the Oath, the common Peripheral Code rulings, Marches, Wizard War, Certamen, the Houses, Quaesitors, Redcaps and the Order's history; that Mystery Cults exist; and in outline the Arts, Parma Magica, Arcane Connections and vis. He cannot teach or cast, but copied such texts for Pompius. He may recognize Aegis of the Hearth, Frosty Breath of the Spoken Lie, Whispers Through the Black Gate, Demon's Eternal Oblivion and various Wards by their effects (Ant p. 40).

He once bitterly envied the Gift, and blames that on his own failing, perhaps helped by the Gift's effect on others. He says little of his family for fear of threats, though threats would not sway him, and he accepts he may die in office (Ant pp. 39, 42, 49). He holds Holy Magic and Hermetic magic to be two cathedrals, one built by angels and one by men, both to God's glory (Ant p. 39). He is not mind-proof: Hermetic magic can ruin his mind or turn him from his mission (Ant p. 48).

The pope may not expect him to succeed; his failure could be the pretext for harsher measures against the Order. Whether God favors his mission is for the troupe to decide (Ant pp. 38-39).

characters.name: Pompius of House Guernicus
characters.summary: A Quaesitor and archmage, in his last years a bright-eyed, lively old man with bent and wiry limbs, much sought to judge, investigate and advise. In the summer of 1202 he turned to stone in the midst of an investigation and passed into Final Twilight. A nearby covenant recovered the statue, and his case notes went to his successor.
characters.secrets:
He made Joseph a Longevity Ritual and spent long talks with him on the place of Order and Church in the Divine plan (Ant p. 39). The Quaesitorial records of his cases hold Joseph's signature, a Sympathetic Connection to the legate (ArM5 p. 84; Ant p. 42).

Perhaps Joseph was somebody's pawn from his notary days on (Ant pp. 41, 49).

characters.name: Brother Peter
characters.summary: A black-habited friar, common-born and cheerful, with a ready store of Scripture. He keeps up a running banter with Brother Bartholomew, whom he resembles so closely that they could be kin, and he speaks the diocese's language as his own.
characters.secrets: More the theologian of the pair, with a great memory for Scripture (p. 59). See The Friars Preacher for his statistics.

characters.name: Brother Bartholomew
characters.summary: A black-habited friar who plays the fool to draw a crowd, with a practised pratfall and a head-over-heels tumble. He is so like Brother Peter that they could be brothers by blood, and his banter puts people at their ease.
characters.secrets: His clowning and common manners hide a keen mind and an academic training (p. 59). See The Friars Preacher for his statistics.

characters.name: Brother Alonso
characters.summary: A black-habited friar from a distant kingdom, with a thick accent and no visible humour. He seems a little sinister, gives no quarter to sin, and likes to describe the torments of sorcerers in Hell in fine detail.
characters.secrets: He understands the local tongue better than he lets on, and uses his seeming ignorance to keep his distance from the others (p. 59). He may come from Aragon or Sicily; rename him Alan if he is from northern Europe. See The Friars Preacher for his statistics.

characters.name: Turstan
characters.summary: A local scoundrel of the diocese, given to drink, dice, loose women and shady deals.
characters.secrets:
The bishop's near-identical double (p. 63) and his Mistaken Identity Flaw. Orris has not worked out that he exists. If confronted he claims to be a con man with a chance likeness, but he is bound up with the curse, and what he is depends on who laid it: a diabolist taking the bishop's form to undo his works, the faerie tormentor dropping in to watch its victim, or an angel waiting to reveal the curse and set the characters on the road to removing it.

He knows more about the curse than first appears (p. 63).

characters.name: Galerius of House Guernicus

params.detail: protect the Order of Hermes from internal threats
cannot cast under a cloudless sky

description.biography:
Combat: dodge Init 0, Attack n/a, Defense +2, Damage n/a; dagger Init 0, Attack +2, Defense +1, Damage +1. Soak +1. Fatigue levels OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wounds -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Equipment: opal ring talisman, wizardly robes, two-minute hourglass, dagger. Encumbrance 0.

Appearance: tall, thin and austere, with the manner of a man used to being obeyed and little patience for talk. He wears robes of good wool worked with gold thread.

His Magic Theory is printed 6 (12): score 6 with 12 experience toward 7. The book asks the troupe to change his native tongue and his Civil and Canon Law specialty to suit the saga (p. 68).

The Definitive Edition's spells are used, which differ from this block (p. 68): The Whole from the Part is level 20 here, printed 15; Disguise of the Transformed Image is level 15 here, printed 10. Maintaining the Demanding Spell at level 20, a general spell. 'Aura of Beguiling Presence', cited to Houses of Hermes: Societates p. 96, is that page's Aura of Beguiling Appearance; 'Words of Unbroken Silence' is Words of the Unbroken Silence.

The block's casting totals check against his Arts, Stamina and Mastery but for two: The Whole from the Part is printed +22, where they give +23, and By His Works +21, where they and the memory attunement give +22 (p. 68).

characters.summary:
A respected Quaesitor of middle rank in the local Tribunal, known for his unflagging work against wrongdoers and as an expert on dealings with mundanes. People say that everyone he has ever looked into turned out guilty of something.

He was the pupil of the great Paulinus, a Quaesitor remembered for his legal opinions and his gift for making peace, whom a mob hanged as a witch while he travelled alone. Galerius traced the careless magus whose public spells had stirred up that town and had him convicted, and has spent the twenty years and more since prosecuting magi he thinks endanger the Order.

He has won cases at several meetings of the Tribunal and has never lost a magus he charged. Many applaud him and privately fear him; he has no known friends but Ingrid of Tremere, and perhaps his own covenant.
characters.secrets:
He believes reckless conduct will bring the Order down, imagines how any small incident could become a disaster, and assumes magi are always scheming round the Code. He cares for the harm a deed might do, not the harm it did, and thinks it better to risk punishing the innocent than to let the guilty go (pp. 67-69).

Under it lies guilt. He worships Paulinus's memory so highly he can never match it, and he has moved the blame for the death onto the Tribunal and his fellow Quaesitors, whose laxity he condemns. His motives are sincere: brought to see that his zeal has made a travesty of justice, he is crushed and tries to make amends (p. 69).

He is seldom seen in his true shape. He favours Disguise of the Transformed Image: a beggar, a leper, a pilgrim, a street urchin, a tradesman's boy on an errand, a peddler, a labourer, any villager he has seen going the other way; a woman if he must. He may change several times a day. His sigil is the colour grey, so every guise has some grey hair or clothing, which can give him away (pp. 68, 71).

His talisman's Invisibility he saves for getting out of trouble, though a major suspect may tempt him. With mundanes he confirms a witness with Posing the Silent Question, casts Trust Me to talk past his Gift, bribes if that fails, and prefers to watch faces as they answer. He lies freely about who he is, and only admits to being a magus hunting 'outlaw wizards' to someone who has already seen magic. The mundanes' distrust of magi seeps into him, and he comes away thinking his suspects rogues (pp. 72-73).

Nightwing keeps watch on crime scenes and scouts for him. Using the raven so, using a disguise to learn about a magus, and walking behind one invisible all count as scrying. His investigation immunity covers only a reasonable suspicion, and he stretches it to gather background on suspects, which the player magi can charge him with if they prove it. He stops short of hard rules: he never turns Intellego Mentem on a magus or a magus's servant without leave (pp. 71-73).

links.note: Convicted and banished from the Tribunal

characters.name: Ingrid of House Tremere

invented_spells.name: Endurance of the Berserkers (Duration: Diameter)
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Antagonists.

description.biography:
Combat: dagger Init +1, Attack +5, Defense +4, Damage +3. Soak +2. Fatigue levels OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wounds -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Equipment: unassuming dress, Ash Wand talisman, dagger. Encumbrance 0.

Appearance: when she travels with Galerius she passes as his wife or daughter, quiet and watchful, in good plain clothes with hardly any jewelry. A second look finds her wiry and athletic, too much so for almost any woman of any rank. She keeps her talisman up her sleeve and has a habit of fingering it.

Her Endurance of the Berserkers is the book's variant, Duration Diameter in place of Concentration (p. 74).

characters.summary:
A junior maga of House Tremere who does not yet hold her voting sigil. Her superiors lend her to the Quaesitors when asked, and she often travels with Galerius as his bodyguard through dangerous country or on violent cases. She stays at his side and says little, though her Gift makes it hard to go unnoticed.

She goes by her Christian name, which cannot serve as a sympathetic connection to her.
characters.secrets:
Rather like a very junior Hoplite, a word she would not use. She is weak at investigation and adds little to the case itself. She deters attacks on Galerius, but if the players do fight, she is less deadly than a true Hoplite (p. 74).

In a fight she opens with The Crystal Dart; if Magic Resistance stops that she turns to indirect spells such as Invisible Sling of Vilano and Pit of the Gaping Earth. Wizard's Leap, mastered, takes her out of danger at fast-cast speed. With both an Arcane and a sympathetic connection to a foe she can penetrate with her favourites, Invocation of Weariness and Grip of the Choking Hand: not lethal, so unlikely to bring a charge of a high crime even without enough cause (p. 74).

If Galerius falls into disgrace, House Tremere presses her to drop him, whatever she thinks herself (p. 79).

characters.name: Paulinus of House Guernicus
characters.summary: A dead Quaesitor of high renown, remembered for his learned legal opinions, his skill as a peacemaker and decades of selfless service. Peasants in a town frightened of witchcraft took him for a witch while he travelled alone; they hunted him through every change of shape, seized him and hanged him in the square.

characters.name: Holger Rosmer of House Jerbiton
characters.summary: The careless magus whose spells cast in public frightened a town and set its bishop preaching against witchcraft, in the troubled days when Paulinus passed through. Galerius hunted him down and charged him with endangering the Order; after a short trial he was convicted and punished with the death of his familiar. Galerius had pressed for a Wizard's March.

characters.name: Kraxia of House Criamon
characters.summary: Accused of molesting the fae, she was shown to have been framed by a neighbour, but Galerius went on to find that she had helped a local bandit escape the mundane authorities, and she was convicted of interfering with mundanes. Her penalty came to several seasons of service.

characters.name: Jürgen of Trier
characters.summary: A magus of Ex Miscellanea who framed his neighbour Kraxia to hide a crime of his own, and whose covenant was afterwards robbed by the bandit she had helped. Galerius exposed him; his penalty came to several seasons of service.

characters.name: Iana of House Merinita
characters.summary: Accused of refusing the outcome of a certamen she lost to Claudius of Verditius. Convicted of that and of obstructing a Quaesitor's investigation, she was banished from the Tribunal, and the lab text of the spell she had used was seized and destroyed.
characters.secrets: With no outside witnesses, she and Claudius each swore under Frosty Breath of the Spoken Lie to having won. Galerius found she had a spell of Momentary duration made to beat truth detection, much like Clear Breath of the Consummate Liar (Guardians of the Forests p. 73), castable without voice or gesture and so brief that it did not show when she was checked for active magic before her testimony. Since then he has insisted on checks before and after any questioning (pp. 75-77).

characters.name: Claudius of House Verditius
characters.summary: The magus who beat Iana of Merinita at certamen, in the case Galerius investigated when she would not honour the result.

characters.name: Tranio of House Jerbiton
characters.summary: Repeatedly accused of stealing vis. Another Quaesitor looked into him without bringing charges; Galerius convicted him.
characters.secrets: Galerius waited invisible at a vis source Tranio had been robbing and caught him at it. The Tribunal's records say he had mundanes watching to tell him when to set the trap; they are not named and never testified (p. 76).

characters.name: Hannelore

description.biography:
Combat: dagger Init +1, Attack +5, Defense +4, Damage +2. Soak -1. Fatigue levels OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wounds -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Equipment: fine clothes, curved dagger. Encumbrance 0 (0).

Appearance: a good-looking young woman, bareheaded, her dark hair waving over green eyes. Red velvet is her choice of dress, under a fur cloak she is seldom without, for she feels the cold. Men remember her voice above all, which is full and low.

characters.summary:
The favoured daughter of Baron Hugo, raised in comfort by a doting father and taught by private tutors, who noticed her temper and ambition and prayed for whoever marries her. She is educated, eloquent and sure of herself, and the Gift does not trouble her. She loves hawking and courtly romances.

She has never married. Those proposed for her fall ill, meet with accidents or disappear, and people find they cannot bear to stay long in her company.
characters.secrets:
Attracted to power, she reads the jealousy the Gift stirs as power's natural effect, and fixes on a magus who seems strong (p. 85). She is infatuated with him and his power; he may love her, she does not love him. Her target is best not repulsive, and need not be a man. Variants: avarice (she wants to be taught, impossible without the Gift) or envy (she wants his magic from him); a male Hannelore; a same-sex pursuit, kept secret, where Hugo might seek no clemency; a companion or storyguide character as target, whom she can enslave and later curse at Arcane Range from connections taken while she held him, watching in crow form if he dwells within an Aegis; a weaker version, with a Power or her vis taken away, keeping Diablerie; a stronger one, with a coven, demons and corrupted beasts in pact, or more Powers; a one-time threat with no prior romance, going straight to her death and return (pp. 80, 84-85).

From a block of forbidden books she initiated herself into the Unholy Method of Incantation, at the cost of a Warping point. The rite drew a powerful demon in a pleasing form, who taught her for five years, feeding her instability with its Obsession power. She knows her power is illicit but does not at first know it is Infernal, or that her beloved's is not (p. 87). She has more Virtues than creation allows: demonic tutelage equal to Mentored by Demons five times (RoP: Infernal p. 86), 50 extra experience a year, and Vituperations that gave her Self-Confident and Aging Points. Such an outlay suggests Hell plans more for her, and that the infatuation is a distraction (p. 81).

Hierarchy Score 3. Fragile Constitution, Infernal Blessing and Tainted With Evil come from Warping, and Arcane Lore free with Diabolist. Her Warping is so high because she takes Warping to fuel her magic (RoP: Infernal p. 104) and carries lasting effects. Unaffected by The Gift: RoP: Magic p. 47 (p. 81).

Powers from her Infernal Blessing, a Level 25 Debauchery / Phantasm effect (Base 4, +1 Touch, +4 Forsaken) (p. 81). Gaze of the Wolf: with eye contact she fixes a person in place while she holds the stare; Penetration 5 + Penetration Bonus + Aura Modifier. The text calls this her Transfix power (pp. 83, 88). Exhaustion: her touch inflicts a Long-Term Fatigue level; not in the Dominion or on women; Penetration as above.

Her vis (p. 81): at least 3 + simple die pawns at any time, some turned to vis prava. Not Personal Vis Sources, as it is never automatic. She steals the Host at Communion and profanes it (RoP: Infernal p. 96); has replaced the relic in her father's chapel with a fake and profaned the true one; contests the spring's vis; and has the beads on one book of her father's.

Casting (p. 82): Communication + Incantation + Power + Aura modifier + stress die. Her Hierarchy spares her the harsh effects of a failed maleficium of level 30 or below. Each use costs a Confidence point, adding nothing, or a Warping point. Range Personal, Duration Forsaken maleficia are taken as already cast (And the Devil, Black Wings, She Who Bears the Mark); each gives a Warping point a year, not included in her score. Bonuses: +5 a pawn of vis prava or +2 of other vis (at most Incantation + Power pawns); +3 a Confidence point (at most 2); +6 for sacrificing a black animal; +5 an assistant at Communication +1 and Incantation 4 (at most 3 with Diablerie, 2 otherwise). With Diablerie, her best Power, around 53 + stress die with Infernal aura 2, 2 Confidence, 4 pawns of vis prava and a black goat; +15 with a coven of 3. See RoP: Infernal chapter 10.

Her maleficia (pp. 82-83) are not formulaic, and she may vary Range, Duration, Target or effect:
A Crown of Twelve Stars on Her Head (Psychomachia, level 40; R Voice, D Moon, T Ind; Base 15, +2 Voice, +3 Moon): the target obeys her commands for the duration, but must be able to see her, hear her voice or smell her perfume, or it ends at once. Usually laid with vis and a sacrifice on a victim she already holds.
A Ghost on the Wind I Shall Become / No Door Can Stop Me (Diablerie, 45; R Per, D Sun, T Ind; Base 35, +2 Sun): the Nightwalker Major Virtue (Hedge Magic Revised Edition p. 104) until sunrise. Her spirit leaves her prone body and travels at great speed, changing between corporeal and immaterial in three rounds, and invisible at will when immaterial. Corporeal she can lift what she could normally carry, which then goes immaterial with her. People near her spirit grow drowsy, and sleepers cannot be woken. Spells on ghosts or spirits affect her, but with no Might she cannot be warded off or laid to rest. She cannot enter the Dominion so.
And the Devil Shall Take Care of His Own (Diablerie, 40; R Per, D Forsaken, T Ind; base effect, +4 Forsaken): Magic Resistance 25, not stacking with other sources.
Black Wings, Eye-Piercing Beak (Diablerie, 35; R Per, D Forsaken, T Ind; Base 15, +4 Forsaken): a False Power copying Skinchanger, crow shape. Her focal item is a fetish made of the wings of the bird she sacrificed.
Blood and Body of the Beast (Diablerie, 35; R Touch, D Mom, T Ind; Base 30, +1 Touch): a short mockery of the Eucharist turning a pawn of vis to vis prava (RoP: Infernal p. 19), worth +5 a pawn to her, not +2.
Break Not, Bend Not, Burn Not / Thy Powers Desert (Diablerie, 25; R Touch, D Sun, T Ind; base effect, +1 Touch, +2 Sun): one object, not living and no larger than a base Individual of its Form, gains Magic Resistance 15, not stacking.
Clothed in the Dragon's Scales (Diablerie, 50; R Per, D Moon, T Ind; Base 35, +3 Moon): a False Power copying Greater Immunity, chosen for the peril, fire being the obvious one. Its level means she can really try only once, with a heavy sacrifice, much vis or a good Ceremony bonus. Could she reach level 55 she would make it Forsaken.
Her Iniquities Shall Be Hidden From His Eyes (Psychomachia, 25; R Eye, D Moon, T Ind; Level 5, +1 Eye, +3 Moon): the target mistakes one thing for something else, a man for a serving maid, a malefic casting for a country dance.
Mother Lilith, Queen of Desire / Stroke his Staff, Stoke the Fire (Psychomachia, 25; R Eye, D Sun, T Ind; Base 10, +1 Eye, +2 Sun): burning lust. She cannot direct the victim but can work him like an addict. Usually follows her power to hold him still.
Pact of the Chalice of Blood (Diablerie, 25; R Voice, D Moon, T Ind; Base 4, +2 Voice, +3 Moon): solemnizes an uncoerced pact with an intelligent creature of Infernal Might, both drinking a sacrifice's blood; it must keep the terms to the letter. Such as a Fimus (RoP: Infernal p. 68), a Fictilis (p. 69) or Morrighu (pp. 72-73) are within her power.
She Who Bears the Mark Shall Be Unharmed (Diablerie, 35; R Per, D Forsaken, T Ind; Base 15, +4 Forsaken): a False Power copying Lesser Immunity, perhaps several times over, to long swords or another weapon, or to magical fire or the like. Each costs resources and Warping, so she may leave a gap; she has likely not guarded against her love's favourite magic, thinking he would never attack her.
The Scorched Heart of a Man Obsessed (Malediction, 35; R Eye, D Moon, T Ind; Base 15, +1 Eye, +3 Moon): the Obsessed Flaw, fixed on her. Near her he can only attend on her; away, she fills his thoughts. Often laid once she has already bewitched him.
The Wrath of Woman Scorches the Valor of Man (Malediction, 35; R Voice, D Sun, T Ind; Base 15, +2 Voice, +2 Sun): overwhelming Fear of women, as the Flaw.
Thy Health Shall Shrivel Like Straw in a Flame (Malediction, 30; R Eye, D Sun, T Ind; Level 5, +1 Eye, +2 Sun, +1 extra point, +1 to lower the minimum): Stamina down 2, to no less than -1, with sudden pain and a hacking cough, trembling heart or other small ailment for the duration.
Trampled Under Death's Pale Hooves (Malediction, 30; R Eye, D Sun, T Ind; base effect, +1 Eye, +2 Sun): -6 to all Ride rolls and 6 extra botch dice on a 0. This and its like for other Abilities are how she disposes of unwanted suitors.

Tactics (pp. 88-90): a maleficium is very obvious, all chanted blasphemies, so she uses Gaze of the Wolf first unless she has surprise. She times incantations for sunrise or sunset, when the Parma Magica lapses. She is no match for a group of magi, with low Penetration against those she has no interest in, but curses companions and grogs with Minor Flaws such as Noncombatant, Palsied Hands or Fear, or blights an Ability or Characteristic, all deliverable at Duration Diameter. She fights hit and run from spirit form, leaves in crow shape, and may bring minor demons under a pact, or a former suitor ensorceled with A Crown of Twelve Stars. His name, and any letters in his own hand, are sympathetic connections she holds to her love.

Redemption (p. 89): she is not beyond it. A patient character, perhaps with the baron, may bring her to see the source of her power and give it up. Abandoned after a true wish to repent, she relapses and seeks revenge. Her wish will be tested by God and fought by her patron; penance means a nunnery.

characters.name: Lady Ermengarde
characters.summary: The wife of Baron Hugo and Hannelore's stepmother.
characters.secrets: She may be a sorceress herself, the true owner of the books, using Hannelore as a cat's-paw to hide her own evil and having corrupted her (p. 87). As a ghost Hannelore possesses her, stirs her and Hugo with Infatuation, fakes or uncovers an infidelity, and drives her with Revenge to kill him; she dies under arrest, her soul forsaken (p. 93).

characters.name: Father Fulke
characters.summary: The priest assigned to the pastoral care of the nuns.
characters.secrets: No priest at all, but an infernalist posing as one, sworn to the demon who trained Hannelore and told to help her. If she is to escape quickly he corrupted the nunnery before she came, drawing younger nuns into rebellion and licence by personal influence (RoP: Infernal pp. 22-23) (p. 91).

characters.name: Friar or Monk of the Abbey

description.biography:
Combat: Dodge Init +3, Defense +4. Club Init +3, Attack +4, Defense +3, Damage +4. Staff Init +4, Attack +6, Defense +6, Damage +3. Soak +2.

Fatigue: OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wound Penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Equipment: Monk's habit, sandals, walking stick (club). Encumbrance 0 (0).

The book prints one block with choices: Mendicant Friar or Priest; Well-Traveled, for a member who has gone out on the abbot's tasks, or Long-Winded; and Abilities and a stick marked for a friar. Its Native Language has no specialty.

characters.summary: A typical brother of the abbey in a woollen robe, trusted in the district. He sees to the house's daily needs and maintenance, or walks the roads on errands for its abbot. The abbot, he says, beat the dragon and lies recovering.
characters.secrets: These are the bulk of the dragon's servants, and few know what their abbot is. The senior priests do, and keep up the story.

characters.name: The Prior of the Abbey

description.biography:
Combat: Dodge Init +3, Defense +4. Soak +2.

The book prints Dodge Init +3 and Defense +4 though his Quickness is -2 and Brawl 2; the figures are entered as printed.

Fatigue: OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wound Penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Equipment: Monk's habit, sandals, walking stick. Encumbrance 0 (0).

The tiers of Vow are not printed: taken as Minor, which balances his Virtues and Flaws.

characters.summary: He acts for the bedridden abbot: dealing with outside officials, supervising the monks and running the house, which he does excellently. Trusted locally and thought wise across the region, he may seem friendly and genial, brusque, or distant and calculating.
characters.secrets:
He knows. Choose his kind. A sincere man inspired by a miracle, Peter to the dragon's messiah. A faithless pragmatist who sees what a real miracle can do. Or a man unbalanced by a Divine act who might go either way, Paul or Judas: as a betrayer he goes on serving, collecting records, secretly asking for help, and learning weaknesses for those who would truly kill it.

He inspects the sleeping quarters and dines with guests in the abbot's place, and may be elected abbot to front for the dragon.

characters.name: Penitent Knight

description.biography:
Combat: Dodge Init +1, Defense +5. Lance and shield (mounted) Init +3, Attack +14, Defense +12, Damage +10. Long sword and shield (mounted) Init +3, Attack +15, Defense +14, Damage +11. Long sword and shield Init +3, Attack +12, Defense +11, Damage +8. Mace and shield Init +2, Attack +10, Defense +9, Damage +10. Soak +14.

Fatigue: OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wound Penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Equipment: War horse, full chain mail, heater shield, lance, long sword, mace. Encumbrance 2 (4).

His men-at-arms: one grizzled veteran (ArM5 p. 21) and four standard soldiers (ArM5 p. 22). The tiers of his Flaws are not printed: the Personality Flaws are taken as Minor, which balances his Virtues and Flaws.

characters.summary: A lone knight in a black surcoat, of stoic bearing, with good gear and a good horse, known locally as pious and more widely as wrathful. He wears the black until his quest is done, to show his sinful state, and leads a small band of men-at-arms.
characters.secrets: He does not know what the abbot is. He seeks absolution for a wrong done on his travels, believes this task will win it, and cannot be talked out of it. He is met recovering an item or harvesting a vis site for the dragon.

characters.name: Acumenis
characters.summary: A magus of Ex Miscellanea who keeps a journal.
characters.secrets: The book gives no more than this. The journal describes Rasa at length, in a converted scriptorium (p. 108), so its writer has met the Dragon Abbot face to face.

characters.name: The Germanic Princess
characters.summary: A barbarian princess of the days of Rome's expansion, tall and red-haired with piercing blue eyes, and fond above all of a single gold and glass bead.
characters.secrets: The book prints no stats and no name. She is held by the Queen's Spirit Away, in a mirror, in the Queen's realm, and the Queen wears her form. If the Queen is killed she can be pulled from the heart-shaped mirror. She wears the bead that is the Queen's real anchor, which gives her the effect of Aura of Rightful Authority (Ant pp. 122-123).

characters.name: The Actor
characters.summary: A player of some talent, who has been called away to a new part by the same patron every few years since his youth.
characters.secrets:
Mortal pawns have no printed stats (Ant p. 124). When he was very young, in his first big role, a patron paid his way, then had him pose as a grieving husband to get a locket of hair from a corpse. Every four years since, the patron has returned with a harder imposture. The one time he refused, not even his friends knew him until the job was done (p. 128).

Taken in a nearby town, he confesses all and says he had no choice. Left too long, he is taken to another kingdom and set new tasks by the Queen's Steward, to help perfect her Distinguished Spy.

characters.name: The Leader of the Cult of the Serpent
characters.summary: The persuasive head of the Cult of the Serpent.
characters.secrets: A hedge wizard with The Gentle Gift, Magical Blood of the serpent and a selection of serpent-related powers, somehow kin to the brood. The book prints no statistics. (p. 136)

books.name: The Baron's Diary
books.author: Baron Giraud Le Cornu
books.description:
A private journal in the baron's own hand.

Secrets
Hidden under the altar of the keep's chapel. It holds every report from his spies and grows into a full profile of the covenant: its people, defenses, floor plan, visitors and income. He adds all he can learn of the magi's magic: their vis sources as far as he knows them, each magus's spells seen cast, their Wizard's Sigils, and his guesses at how to break or avoid a spell. Most of it is guesswork or misunderstanding, but about a quarter is true, enough to make him dangerous (Ant p. 29).

books.name: The Order of Hermes
books.author: Father Joseph of Napoli
books.description: Written at San Giovanni Maggiore for clerical readers, and circulating in the Church, especially the curia.

books.name: The Rule of The Order of Hermes
books.author: Father Joseph of Napoli
books.description: An account of the Order's law, written at San Giovanni Maggiore for clerical readers. The book calls the subject Code of Hermes Lore.

books.name: History of the Magi of the Ecclesiastical Province of Rome
books.author: Father Joseph of Napoli
books.description: A regional history of the Order, written at San Giovanni Maggiore for clerical readers.

books.name: The Legate's Letters of Authority
books.description:
Letters under papal seal, kept in a leather scroll case. They name Father Joseph as legate and envoy to the Order, with free and safe passage, the right to speak with magi for the pope, and power to requisition help from churches, bishops and monasteries.

Secrets
He shows them to the bishop of each new diocese, who sends a well-known deacon or priest with him, for his credit and to watch him, as bishops fear an audit; the deacon goes on with him to the next diocese. A bishop who truly thinks the Order heretical or Infernal may hinder him (Ant p. 43). Intelligence + Church Lore against Ease Factor 9 knows or guesses he has them. InAn (ArM5 p. 117) shows they came from the curia, probably by a scribe. They only record his powers: losing them costs him no authority and gives a thief none, though a careful impostor could use them. Fresh ones mean returning to Rome, unless he left a set with a friendly bishop (Ant pp. 43-44).

books.name: Eight other tractatus
books.description: Eight more tractatus on Theology, Civil & Canon Law and Organization Lore: Church, all of Quality 7. The book does not say how many are on each subject (p. 52).

books.name: Baron Hugo's Forbidden Books
books.description:
A set of books the baron keeps locked in a chest in his chamber and has forbidden his daughter to read.

Secrets
A corpus of diabolic lore, Infernal Lore at the least; the library may also hold tomes on the maleficia, the Goetic Arts, hedge wizardry or even Hermetic magic. No Level or Quality is printed. They are entered under Hannelore, who reads them in secret, because a baron cannot own a book here. One has glass beads on its cover, each holding a pawn of vis (pp. 81, 87).

familiars.name: Nightwing
familiars.species: A raven, the Raven of Virtue

creatures.name: Dorothy Anning
creatures.appearance: A wise woman of the baron's council.
creatures.notes: The book prints no statistics.
creatures.secrets: A faerie in the guise of a wise woman, with pretenses and powers in place of magical ability, who has joined the council to learn how men use their power for the good of others.

creatures.name: The Finger Bone of Saint Jerome

powers.name: Faithful Wisdom
powers.description: Blesses someone to read one text named at the blessing (tractatus, summa, Lab Text or the like), whatever their literacy, language or script, at a normal reader's pace, with the text in hand. Anyone literate may also copy it, without error, by the normal rules; the copy is exact, not a translation, so they may not read it afterward.

creatures.appearance: A saint's finger bone on a silver chain, worn under the robes round Father Joseph's neck. Saint Jerome, patron of scholars, who translated the Vulgate, is known to anyone with a score in Church Lore.
creatures.notes:
A relic, not a being, held here for its Might and powers: 1 Faith Point and Divine Might 10, which gives its bearer Magic Resistance (ArM5 p. 189; RoP:D pp. 43-46). Its powers run on its Might, which returns each sunrise. The book prints no Might Form. Intellego Vim with enough Penetration gives a rough idea of its powers (Ant p. 42).

To scale it, raise its Faith to 2 or 3 for a total Magic Resistance of 35 or 45, perhaps with more powers, or swap Faithful Wisdom for another; RoP:D p. 88 has more (Ant pp. 43, 49). The book's two examples, not on the bone as printed:

Life of the Ascetic: 5 points, Init +3, Corpus, R Touch, D Sun, T Individual. The one blessed feels hunger and thirst but takes no harm from going without food or drink.

Rebuke of the Scholar: 1 point, Init +10, Corpus, R Voice, D Sun, T Individual. A curse of stammering that bars coherent speech. A caster takes the penalty for casting without words, but can still make noise, so Voice spells keep their range.

creatures.name: Abaissier
creatures.order: Lord of the Avengers of Evil
creatures.weakness: Protected group: people who whip themselves in a way the Church allows.

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Builds a solid body out of the world's ambient, unformed matter; the Appearance says what it looks like.

powers.name: Envisioning
powers.description:
For 1 point the demon enters and twists a dream; for 5 it makes a waking hallucination. One meant to terrify is ignored on a Brave roll of 9+, and failing brings on a violent bodily reaction such as a seizure.

Abaissier likes to show people some tiny failing, to feed their Pride with the thought that a little flagellation would make them perfect. These visions are resisted on a Humble roll of 9+.

powers.name: Protective Obsession
powers.description: Costs 1 to 3 points. If it beats Magic Resistance while someone commits a sinful thought or deed, that person gains a temporary Self-loathing trait, and at the next chance rolls against a suitable trait to avoid harming or punishing himself. If the Obsession fails the trait goes; if it wins the trait is permanent. A person under it has a Light Wound modifier of +1, stacking for no more than three wounds (+3).

powers.name: Punish the Sinner
powers.description: Delivered by touch, and usable with a blow of the flail. If it penetrates, an unexpiated mortal sin causes a Heavy wound and a venial sin a Light wound. Someone with no obvious sin takes damage equal to the sum of his negative Personality Traits.

creatures.appearance: An angel whose body is chain on fire, coloured like old blood and brass. Its pale robe, alone among its kind, shows a stain like blood when it is hurt. It has no right hand, only five slender chains with weights at their tips, which run out to a startling length in a fight and strike each for itself.
creatures.notes:
Wound Penalties as printed: +1* (1-7), -3 (8-14), -5 (15-22), Incapacitated (23-30), Dead (31+). *Light wounds make him more dangerous: he may hurt himself each round for the bonus, which cannot pass +5.

Cost of Envisioning: 1 or 5 points. Cost of Protective Obsession: 1 to 3 points.

The block calls his order the Avengers of Evil; his text calls him a Lord of the Angels of Punishment. Vis: the book gives 7 pawns, one in each whip, and five chains.
creatures.secrets:
A demon of Pride who turns the very pious from God: suffer more, he says, and you are more beloved of Him. It is false, and the more people have given up, the harder it is to admit it. He tempts single believers and seduces charismatic men who then lead small heretical groups, and he makes sinners harm themselves and think they have atoned. As a Lord he commands many lesser demons.

He brings several cells into the open at once so they are hard to stamp out, then forces the weaker Fabrico into servitude. When the Church or the magi move, he stays out of sight and will sacrifice Fabrico if it shows him who his enemies are and how they work. He signs his work: the red mark on the flagellants' robes is a cult symbol he has used before.

His Pride is his weakness. He underestimates the player characters and can be goaded into a fight; evidence able to destroy the cult's remains may bring him to attack in person.

creatures.name: Bufonia
creatures.weakness: Protected group: people who never drink well-water.

powers.name: Envisioning
powers.description: For 1 point the demon enters and twists a dream; for 5 it makes a waking hallucination. One meant to terrify is ignored on a Brave roll of 9+, and failing brings on a violent bodily reaction such as a seizure.

powers.name: Form of Wickedness
powers.description: Makes a solid form of pure sin, held for one round before she must take spiritual or human form. Those near her without enough Magic Resistance start to suspect their neighbours of poisoning them. Each hour they make a Stamina stress roll of 6+: failing costs a Fatigue level, success breaks the hold, and falling unconscious ends it. A botch brings temporary insanity and a Minor Personality Flaw suited to the sin.

powers.name: Form of The Proud Man
powers.description: Once she has taken corporeal form by Form of Wickedness, she can take her solid form; the Appearance describes it.

powers.name: Possession
powers.description: Variable points. After overcoming Magic Resistance she stores some Might in a temporary pool in the victim, and the possession ends when it is spent. The two parts of her can speak only in sight of each other. She drives the host, but something the victim finds abhorrent costs Might: a stress die plus the Might spent against his Personality trait roll. A Supernatural ability costs 1 Might, or as many as a possessed creature spends on one of its powers.

powers.name: Contagious Obsession
powers.description: 1 point a victim. If it beats Magic Resistance while someone commits a sinful thought or deed, he gains a temporary Hates (group) trait and at the next chance rolls against a suitable trait to avoid trying to harm the scapegoats. If it fails the trait goes; if it wins the trait is permanent. Each victim carries it and can pass it, by the same rolls, to anyone he abuses; every new victim costs her 1 Might. It stops spreading when the carrier runs out of Might or a day passes with nobody infected, though those afflicted stay so.

creatures.appearance: By nature a shapeless darkness, sin given sight. In solid form she passes for a tall lady of good breeding, and often goes in the dress of a plague doctor.
creatures.notes:
Thrown vial: touching the undiluted contents is poisoning of Ease Factor 9, doing heavy damage (ArM5 p. 180; Definitive Edition p. 406).

Soak: +1 in human form, entered here; the book also prints Toad form +3, though no power or appearance gives her a toad form.

Wound Penalties as printed: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Her vis lies in a long nose, which neither of her printed shapes mentions.

The plague (p. 100). With the disease rules of Art & Academe pp. 47-50: Severity 13, Stable 9, Improve 12, interval a week, causing a Heavy Wound. Otherwise use ArM5 p. 180 and treat it as a poison of Ease Factor 12 causing a Major Wound. The symptoms are thirst and burning in the fingertips, nose and toes, then bleeding from the eyes and ears.

The plague need not be the Black Death. The book suggests something the players think of as mild, such as measles or scarlet fever, or symptoms they cannot name.

links.note: Poisons wells beside it, for her own ends

creatures.secrets:
She teaches people to poison wells, and never does it herself, so that a scapegoat takes the hatred: Jews, lepers, pagans, Muslims, sorcerers and, her own passion, greengrocers. In human form she tells some dupes their brews protect against plague. They drink it strong to save themselves and soon die, and she so enjoys telling them whom they have killed that she keeps a few such victims when willing helpers would do more harm.

For this plague each potion needs a human heart, best from a plague death. Neither ally nor servant of Abaissier, she thinks Fabrico rules the flagellants and does not fear him. Once the processions begin she recruits poisoners in towns near them to destroy whichever outsiders come easiest, magi included, and if strong opposition appears she wants Fabrico blamed. Their evils fit so well they seem to be working together.

She can brew many diseases and may change them to avoid being caught, but must not show more range than Fabrico could (p. 100).

creatures.name: Fabrico

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Builds a solid body out of the world's ambient, unformed matter; the Appearance says what it looks like.

powers.name: Delusion
powers.description: Vivid illusions: 1 point for a single object, 5 for one the size of a room. Each has some subtle fault. He uses them to fake miraculous messages.

powers.name: Duplicate the Magi's Creation or Transmutation
powers.description: Variable cost and Form. Does any non-ritual Creo or Muto Hermetic spell of level 20 or lower; he uses it with props to make false relics.

powers.name: Envisioning
powers.description:
For 1 point the demon enters and twists a dream; for 5 it makes a waking hallucination. One meant to terrify is ignored on a Brave roll of 9+, and failing brings on a violent bodily reaction such as a seizure.

Fabrico often uses waking dreams to counterfeit visions, resisted with a suitable Personality Trait roll of 9+.

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: Costs 1 to 3 points. If it beats Magic Resistance while someone commits a sinful thought or deed, he gains a temporary Gullible trait, and at the next chance rolls against a suitable trait to avoid believing something dangerous or stupid. If it fails the trait goes; if it wins the trait is permanent.

creatures.appearance: Like any deluder, by nature he is a dark tear in things, crowded with eyes, teeth and innards. For this story he goes as a flagellant bound up in bandages.
creatures.notes:
Guile is printed 6+2, the +2 being his Puissant Guile.

Wound Penalties as printed: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Cost of Delusion and Envisioning: 1 or 5 points. Cost of Obsession: 1 to 3 points.

links.note: Claims part of it, then serves Abaissier against his will

creatures.secrets:
He enjoys passing off his work as the Divine: he makes ordinary objects, wraps them in fake miracles until they are hailed as relics, and backs whoever teaches the resulting errors. His little cults believe a saint has chosen them, and that regular signs let them know God's will better than the Church. The Church usually puts them down.

In this story he first spreads prophets of the Antichrist and the world's end, then notices the flagellants and claims part of them. Beaten, he serves Abaissier against his will and knows his master would spend him as a decoy, so the player characters may set him on Abaissier and weaken both. Destroying him does not end the cult, but it costs it the public's love and drives it back, over time, to secret cells.

creatures.name: Small Demons of Rot
creatures.weakness: They cannot harm, and are burned by touching, the Host or wheat meant to become the Host.

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Builds a solid body out of the world's ambient, unformed matter; the Appearance says what it looks like.

creatures.appearance: Little rat-like humanoids that turn up wherever grain is stored and foul it with the pus from their claws.
creatures.notes:
Foes for grogs and companions. Too weak to do much with one blow, they attack in groups; a large group may grapple or blind an opponent while the others try called shots.

Claws: a putrid ichor causes fever and sepsis in a scratch (a disease of Ease Factor 6 causing a minor wound, ArM5 p. 180) and makes plant products moulder and rot.

Wound Penalties as printed: -1 (1), -3 (2), -5 (3), Incapacitated (4), Dead (5+).
creatures.secrets: Abaissier orders them to rot seed corn, to break communities with famine before his preachers arrive.

creatures.name: Malicia
