powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: Costs 1 to 3 points. If it beats Magic Resistance while someone commits a sinful thought or deed, he gains a temporary Self-Harming trait, and at the next chance rolls against a suitable trait to avoid hurting himself. If it fails the trait goes; if it wins the trait is permanent.

powers.name: Envisioning
powers.description: For 1 point the demon enters and twists a dream; for 5 it makes a waking hallucination. One meant to terrify is ignored on a Brave roll of 9+, and failing brings on a violent bodily reaction such as a seizure.

powers.name: Endurance of the Enraged
powers.description: She takes no Wound penalties, except on Defense totals.

powers.name: Waxing of the Humors
powers.description: Passion drowns sense: the victim needs a Personality trait stress roll of 9+ to hold the emotion in check. Often used straight after a successful Obsession.

creatures.appearance: A young woman out of whose breast a snake grows. It worries at her everywhere but the face, leaving small bleeding bites, some of them bruised dark by poison and decay.
creatures.notes:
Berserk: +2 Attack on both lines; Soak +3 in place of +1. The bite is venomous, as an asp's (ArM5 p. 180; Definitive Edition p. 406: Ease Factor 9, Incapacitating).

Wound Penalties as printed: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (15-20), Dead (21+). The book's 15 falls in two ranges; the usual table starts Incapacitated at 16.

Cost of Envisioning: 1 or 5 points. Cost of Obsession: 1 to 3 points.

links.note: Lieutenant, recruited with a promise of prey

creatures.secrets:
A Fury, feeding on the anger that destroys the one who feels it, drawn to the cult by a promise of plenty of prey. Flagellants she takes whip the onlookers and may kill themselves by mistake; leaders she takes may counsel suicide.

She is the lieutenant to set before the player characters so the saga does not close too early in a fight with the main demons. Destroying her slows the cult and weakens it locally, though it still reaches the next stage. If Abaissier falls she tries to seize part of his cult and turn its despair under the crackdown into mass suicide.

creatures.name: Possessed Follower
creatures.notes: A template, not a person: take any suitable grog or companion, give them Infernal Might 10 and the Berserk Virtue, and add +3 to their Soak and +3 to their damage. The book prints no Form for the Might.
creatures.secrets: These attack the counter-processions, and defend the rag manufactory, where bodiless demons help the acolytes fight and work their corpses after death. Some guard the false saints.

creatures.name: Rasa the Dragon Abbot

reputations.name: The Hungry Dragon Who Eats Travelers (several different regions)
The Reclusive Abbot of the Monastery (local)

powers.name: Cleansing Flame
powers.description: A gout of flame 12 paces wide, 12 tall and 55 long; everything in it takes stress die +25 fire damage. CrIg 50 (Base 20, +2 Voice, +4 size): Greater Power (50 levels) and partial Improved Powers (-3 Might cost).

powers.name: Taste of Memory
powers.description: From a creature it eats, Rasa takes a particular memory of an act or event, 5 experience points of a skill, or a Virtue. Skills improve as normal, but the creature must be eaten alive; a Virtue may be taken once a year. Might spent on skills or Virtues also lowers its Might Score, regained with 10 pawns of vis per point or a season's rest, without using the power so, in a Divine aura of 5 or more. Not a Hermetic power: the figures are for mechanics only. PeMe 35 (Base 15, +1 Touch, +1 Cr requisite, +2 complexity): Ritual Power x2 (35 levels, -3 points).

powers.name: Gift of Blood
powers.description: Whoever drinks its blood gains the Tough Virtue until Rasa takes it back or the drinker dies; the Might stays out of its pool until then. Rasa may also heal itself of a Medium Wound or less, and that Might returns normally. No Hermetic equivalent. CrAn 25 (Base 20, +1 Touch): Ritual Power (25 levels).

powers.name: Sign of Peace
powers.description: An incense-scented mist fills the building, and those without Magic Resistance can scarcely do violence or sin: they gain Peaceful +4, Kind +3 and Obedient +3. To act against these, one must fail an Ease Factor 9 roll on the trait, or pass one on an opposing trait at 9 plus the trait's bonus. A grog trying to hurt someone must fail 9+ on Peaceful or make 13+ on Violent, Angry or Vengeful. ReMe 50 (Base 10, +2 Voice, +3 Moon, +3 Structure): Greater Power (50 levels), Improved Powers x2 (initiative).

powers.name: Scale of Truth
powers.description: One of its scales, in plain sight, makes the eyes of anyone in the room flash red for an instant when they lie or quibble. Brothers who know of it look down or shut their eyes to fib, and hold a speaker's gaze when listening. It lasts until Rasa rescinds it, destroying the scale, and the Might does not return until then. InMe 50 (Base 10, +3 Sight, +2 Sun, +2 Room, +1 tethered to object): Greater Power (50 levels).

powers.name: Gift of the Stigmata
powers.description: Rasa imbues a scale and trades it to someone for a lock of hair. Until the next full moon, wounds that person takes while holding it pass to the dragon, which cannot Soak them but judges them on its own scale: a 13-point hit that would be a Heavy Wound on a Size 0 friar is a Light Wound to Rasa. CrCo 75 (Base 35, +4 Arcane Connection, +3 Moon, +1 Rego requisite): Ritual Power x3 (75 levels).

creatures.appearance: A wingless, eight-legged worm of some seventeen paces, of which three are head and eight tail. It is pale as mother-of-pearl at the neck, darkening along the back to the brown of old blood. Its belly hangs near the ground, yet its shoulder is a little over two paces high. Its fangs and talons are dagger-long, and its black, gold-ringed eyes are almost two palms wide. Mist heavy with sandalwood pours from its jaws, which do not move when it speaks, for the voice rises from far within.
creatures.notes:
Wound Penalties as printed: -1 (1-13), -3 (14-26), -5 (27-39), Incapacitated (40-52), Dead (53+). Decrepitude n/a.

Virtues as printed; the book calls Magic Animal 'Magical Animal' and Student of Divine 'Student of Dominion', and gives Rasa one more Minor Virtue of the storyguide's choice. Hunger for Any Magic is Hunger for (Form), but any vis will do. Magical Qualities name claws for Attack, Damage and Defense.

Font of Knowledge (Minor Supernatural Virtue, p. 109): grants the Ability at 1. A roll of Intelligence + Font of Knowledge + stress die against 6 + 3 x the day's earlier uses, failures included, lets it try a task with an untrained Ability as if at score 2. After two uses, Rasa rolls 7 + stress die against 12.

It can squeeze through most ordinary doorways, but no power lets it take human shape. Gift of Blood prints a Touch range and no Duration or Target.

Sign of Peace is printed at 5 points though a 50-level Greater Power would cost 10.

Naming it (p. 109): 'the abbot' keeps the focus on its office; an angelic name stresses the change in it; 'Rasa' stresses the dragon's past. The troupe's choice colours how the characters deal with it.

links.note: Saw it and wrote of it

creatures.secrets:
Once a mere marauding serpent that gained a sliver of what it ate, it grew aware and began to choose: fewer beasts, more villages and caravans. A veteran of the Silk Road sent it east; years there gave it scraps of six tongues. A missionary priest turned it west toward the great cities of the Eastern Empire. It lingered in one place after another for decades, for centuries, until it ate the abbot.

It threatened a remote abbey, and the abbot, a man of True Faith, went out alone to face it. Eating him gave it his understanding and Faith, and an epiphany that changed it. It took his place; the community called it a miracle and serves it devoutly. Its faith is genuine, though its grasp of people and the Divine is secondhand and a little flawed.

It works to widen the Divine, believing that brings people nearer God and the world nearer Paradise: through charity, teaching crafts, and great works. It cares for the other realms only as foils, and may lure their creatures near for its monks to beat. Their texts and artifacts are to be gathered, hidden and at last destroyed. It treats opposition as God's test of its faith and never blames its opponents.

Enemies: a Tremere whose Redcap lover it ate, who raised a vexillation that failed to hunt it; the jinn Howling Knife of the Dunes; and Stellatus (ArM5 p. 194, the Definitive Edition p. 465), who could not transform to stop its attack on a caravan he rode with, and fought it several times in the decades after.

It eats trained birds for what they saw, the reason for the abbey's aviaries, and now and then dogs or cats, with a small prayer of thanks. Because these are natural and non-magical, Parma does not interfere, though neither bird nor dragon knows of it. It must eat vis, so friars harvest lesser sites, knowing that success destroys what it needs.

It buried a hoard at every old lair, full of coin, jewels, weapons and curios. A trusted clergyman or penitent knight goes with a mule and a gift of its blood to fetch them, journeys that may take long, and its plans allow for that. From its stolen memories it also recalls where relics lie.

creatures.name: The Queen of Gold and Glass

powers.name: Allure
powers.description: +3 to every roll to impress or convince others. Base 3, +1 Touch, +2 Sun.

powers.name: Eidolon
powers.description: Makes an illusory figure that moves, acts and speaks at her direction, best of all on something reflective. Base 2, +2 move at direction, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 intricacy.

powers.name: Extend Glamour
powers.description: Constant. Makes a small mundane area part of her kingdom, with no formal boundary needed. There she may change anything cosmetic to suit her theme, summon any servant, sense all that happens and appear anywhere, and the area has a Faerie aura of 6. Fuller in Realms of Power: Faerie. Cost marked Special.

powers.name: Guide
powers.description: Nudges the victims toward a course of action; she uses it to make humans exercise the skills she means to copy. Base 5, +2 Voice, +1 Conc, +2 Group.

powers.name: Hound
powers.description: Tells her how far off her prey is, and in which direction. Base 3, +4 Arc, +1 Conc.

powers.name: Limited Enthrallment
powers.description: Dominates a victim in a trance with one possible order: to gaze at their own reflection without thought. Collapse from exhaustion ends it; so does being shaken, or a hand passed before the eyes. Printed as costing 20 levels from Base 25, +1 Eye, +2 Conc.

powers.name: Spirit Away
powers.description: Described in Realms of Power: Faerie; no Might cost or dice here. Holds the princess in a mirror, lends the Queen her form and powers the frame. She uses it no further in this story.

powers.name: Travel Through Mirrors
powers.description: Lets her step from Faerie into the mortal world through a mirror. Fading back is no power but the nature of all faeries, though most cannot return so fast. Cost marked Greater Powers (Special).

vis.where: in the shards of the heart-shaped mirror
in a gold and glass bead

creatures.equipment: The finery of a barbarian queen of the time of Rome's expansion, all of it glamour that passes for mortal goods.
creatures.appearance:
A tall, broad-shouldered woman who looks to be in her early twenties, red-haired and sharp-eyed, her eyes a vivid blue. Her cloak seems to be bands of leather and spotted hide by turns, pinned by a thorn at the right shoulder, over a close, sleeveless linen dress worked in purple and stout boots tooled along the tops.

She and all she wears are a little see-through, and paler than they ought to be.
creatures.notes:
Wounds as printed (p. 122): -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Broken (16-20), Shattered (21+). Her Stamina 0 is supernaturally tireless. Her Pretenses are any that suit, with Order of Hermes Lore 2, which is why her challenges miss the mark. Her body and props, like any faerie's, are not resisted by Parma Magica (p. 121). Its Abilities are the book's Pretenses.

Attribute Duplication has no Might cost and needs no Penetration (p. 121). Her Soak -9 comes of Supernaturally Fragile.

Traditional Ward (absolute darkness): without Realms of Power: Faerie, she shuns darkness as a vampire shuns garlic. Reflective surfaces, in her powers, are any that show an outline, not detail (p. 123).

Without Realms of Power: Faerie (p. 121): she has a role and no soul, so she must mark her work with repeated insignia, run her victims through a series of stories and face them at the end, and cannot sidestep the story, for instance by paying for what she wants, since she feeds on what they feel along the way.
creatures.secrets:
Long ago, as Rome pushed out over the tribes, a mortal master made a flawless mirror for the woman he loved. She betrayed him, and he cursed it and buried it. A faerie found it and gave it to a princess; when she looked in, the Queen reached through from Faerie and took her shape, her life and her place. Since then the Queen has toyed with mortals and made faerie copies of her foes (Ant p. 120).

She is a dispenser of labours, a faerie fed by the quests she sets. Now she wants one or more of her servants shaped into a court magician, true in every small detail. So she chooses young magi and goads them: every new spell her servants see or suffer is one her wizards can then imitate, and she counts a challenge won if she sees one (p. 120). She does not want the magi dead, and may aid them against third parties. She is immortal and patient; they will know better spells when they are older.

She is highly cognizant, and knows her own role and how far she can exploit it (p. 121). She keeps out of combat for fear of her fragility, and sets minions to fight for her. She tailors those minions to the magi's strength and scatters tokens that lead to her, like a game's final foe; the book means the troupe to enjoy this, and to be rewarded for adding touches that suit it, such as a faerie key that opens any lock, or enemies dying in a shower of coins (p. 121). She has no originality: fill her stories with motifs from the magi's own lives, gathered by her Shadowy Minions (p. 124).

Her weaknesses: faeries who cannot bear mirrors (the smoothfaces, and the knockers, who know much about her); darkness; her glass body. If she is killed, her body breaks into gold-backed glass; the 8 pawns of Imaginem in the largest piece are a decoy. Her true anchor is the bead the princess wears, holding 8 pawns (no Art printed). Unless that vis is taken, she may in time rebuild her body or move to another object (p. 123).

creatures.name: The Frame of Gold

powers.name: Spirit Away
powers.description: Used to carry on the story it was shaped for. The Queen's own Spirit Away powers it (p. 122).

creatures.appearance: Pieces of what seem to be a gilded picture frame.
creatures.notes:
Intellego Vim finds faerie glamour in a piece, and no vis that can be used. Completed and set between two mirrors, it is a corridor to the Land of Gold and Glass; in that form it is a whole faerie, and holds 8 pawns of Rego (Ant p. 124).

Each piece can sense what is round it, speak to the others, move when unwatched and quietly influence its surroundings. It may change the dreams of anyone without Magic Resistance who claims aloud to own it (p. 125). The book prints no Might, Characteristics or Powers for it; it gives none of its Pretenses by name.

A storyguide may make a separate story of the quest for each piece, with clues in place of the pieces (p. 124). The pieces can serve as Arcane Connections to each other (see Breaking the Story).
creatures.secrets: This is no object but a Threshold Guardian, a faerie that longs to be whole. Its pieces lead their owners into each other's reach. A piece lost or destroyed does not matter: the Queen supplies another if she wants the magi to come (Ant pp. 124-125).

creatures.name: The Distinguished Knight

attacks.name: Great sword and mirrored heater shield

powers.name: Damaging Effect
powers.description: Supernaturally sharp: tiny slivers of glass break away and stay in the wound. 2 intricacy points spent on cost. Base 5, +1 Part, +1 Diameter; the book says this Base is lower than Hermetic magic might suggest.

powers.name: Flight
powers.description: Constant. Base 4, +2 Sun, +1 constant, a Base deliberately below what Hermetic magic might suggest.

powers.name: Shift Human Shapes
powers.description: He dons or sheds his armour by willing it. 1 intricacy point spent on cost. Printed as Base 3, +2 Sun, though its Duration is Mom.

vis.where: a rusty piece from human-sized armor

creatures.equipment: Armour of magical scales of faerie iron, a lance with pennant and other weapons, an attendant for a squire, and gear bearing the mirror. His glamour makes a faerie horse.
creatures.appearance:
A towering figure in bright scale armour, who can change into a very large man of surface charm.

His courtesy outdoes that of the humans he imitates, and he loves to call them out to duels over tiny failings of conduct.
creatures.notes: The great sword's Damage includes +5 for Improved Damage and +5 for Damaging Effect. Single Weapon is 9+2; the +2 is Puissant Pretense (the book's Puissant Militant Pretense). The mirrored shield may hold a Hazy Servant. Charm 9 has limits: he has no notion of sex. His horse shares his vis, Might and Magic Resistance and, being glamour, flies when he does. He has more Pretense experience than his Virtues permit, which only a player faerie must balance; he is not designed as one (Ant p. 130). Its Abilities are the book's Pretenses.
creatures.secrets: The Queen's champion, and her last guard if her realm is raided (Ant p. 130).

creatures.name: Undistinguished Warriors

powers.name: Damaging Effect
powers.description: Supernaturally sharp: tiny slivers of glass break away and stay in the wound. 2 intricacy points spent on cost. Base 5, +1 Part, +1 Diameter, a Base below the Hermetic norm.

powers.name: Flight
powers.description: Constant. Base 4, +2 Sun, +1 constant, a Base deliberately below what Hermetic magic might suggest.

powers.name: Shift Human Shapes
powers.description: Dons or sheds armour by will. 1 intricacy point spent on cost. Printed as Base 3, +2 Sun, though its Duration is Mom.

vis.where: a rusty piece from human-sized armor

creatures.equipment: Armour of magical scales of faerie iron.
creatures.appearance: No two are alike: bowman, spearman, swordsman and so on. Some lack limbs, yet walk without a leg and handle arms without a hand, and many lack pieces of the head.
creatures.notes: Each has one of the six listed weapons, not all; every Damage includes +5 for Damaging Effect. The Pretense is printed Single Weapon or Bow 6 (as weapon). They hold more Pretense experience than their Virtues permit, and are not suitable as player faeries (Ant p. 131). Its Abilities are the book's Pretenses.

creatures.name: The Distinguished Herald
creatures.notes:
One of the Distinguished Servants (p. 127).

Pretenses of 9 in what the role needs (p. 130). A symbolic object holding vis is embedded deep in its head; the pawns are not printed. The book prints no Might, Characteristics or Powers for it; it gives none of its Pretenses by name.
creatures.secrets: In the Herbam challenge it steals a Gifted child, gives it to smoothfaces, then spreads the tale among mortals (p. 127).

creatures.notes: Named only as the one who gives the actor his new tasks (p. 128). The book does not say that it is one of the Distinguished. The book prints no Might, Characteristics or Powers for it; it gives none of its Pretenses by name.
creatures.secrets: In the seed Firebrand Tytalus, the Queen is designing a new steward (p. 132).

creatures.name: Undistinguished Servants
creatures.how_many: Many, filling roles next to those of the Distinguished
creatures.appearance: Half made: bits of the body gone or clear as glass, under a faultless human face.
creatures.notes:
Might from 5 to 20 by how near it is to finished, so the Might here shows 0. Pretense 6 in the skills most vital to its role. Powers vary, many of them the Queen's or the Distinguished Knight's (p. 130). A symbolic object holding vis is wedged in its head; the pawns are not printed.

None can break a mirror or attack someone who carries one.
creatures.secrets: They too are being shaped to human roles, and the Queen spends them far more readily than the Distinguished (p. 130).

creatures.name: Undistinguished Magi
creatures.how_many: As suits the story; one per player character is a lot for a short saga
creatures.appearance: Copies of real magi, comic exaggerations at first. After years of shaping, dressed to hide their flaws, they may fool even friends.
creatures.notes:
Undistinguished Servants templated on the player magi, or on two or more at once. They share their models' looks, magic and strongest Personality Traits. The book prints no figures, and three ways to choose their spells: list every spell cast before her minions; note the highest level cast for each Technique and Form pair; or give only signature spells, with spontaneous magic to suit (p. 132).

Intellego Vim would unmask one at once, but to cast it on a magus breaks the Code, and these copies offer no cause (p. 132).
creatures.secrets: They are the point of the whole scheme. See A Faerie Magus? in the last stage of A Run of Odd Troubles.

creatures.name: Hazy Servants
creatures.how_many: Many, at the edges of the court
creatures.appearance: Like people glimpsed far off through smoke or fog, until something greater turns its eye on them, when they spring into shape.
creatures.notes:
A template: any fitting character from any Ars Magica supplement, +10 Faerie Might, with powers from the Queen's or the Distinguished Knight's list. Their Characteristics shift with their roles (p. 130).

One loses focus when ignored, and there is a small delay between being noticed and taking shape. They flee bright, clear light. They alone of her servants can break a mirror, but seem to die in doing so (p. 131). The Knight's shield may hold one (p. 130).

They loose the plague of animals (p. 125).

creatures.name: Shadowy Minions
creatures.appearance: Little more than an afterthought or a plan, a shadow given life.
creatures.notes: No substance and no powers: they can neither touch a thing nor attack anyone. They can still spy, and the sight of one can scare people, set dogs barking or bolt horses (p. 131).
creatures.secrets: They bring the Queen the details of the magi's lives that she recycles in her stories (p. 124). Faerie Lore of 18+ knows of them (p. 129).

creatures.name: Ice Wyrm

powers.name: Conjuration of the Indubitable Cold
powers.description: As the spell of that name, ArM5 p. 142. 3 intricacy points spent on cost.

powers.name: Constrict
powers.description: A hit coils round the victim, who cannot use melee weapons. Damage then comes each round with no Attack roll, but may be Soaked. At the end of each round, the first included, the victim may try to escape: Strength + stress die against the wyrm's. Each helper adds +1 and cannot attack the wyrm that round. Success frees him, to attack as normal next round. Six rounds held (30 seconds) calls for deprivation rolls, ArM5 p. 179.

powers.name: Constant Damaging Effect
powers.description: Constant. Its terrible cold deals +5 Damage each round. Base 5, +1 Part, +2 Sun, +1 Constant.

powers.name: Spreading a Mantle of Ice
powers.description: 3 intricacy points spent on cost. All water freezes for a mile about it, and any rain falls as snow. The air grows so bitter that hunting it takes magic or preparation, though spells that sense warmth can find it, always at the coldest point. The cold being magical, Auram Magic Resistance of 30 or more does not feel it.

powers.name: Venomous Bite
powers.description: When its Attack Advantage beats the victim's armor Protection (not Soak), the victim suffers adder venom (Poison Table, ArM5 p. 180), wound or no wound. The storyguide may shift the Advantage needed.

vis.where: in a piece of lost string

creatures.equipment: A small heap of frozen treasure.
creatures.appearance: A vast serpent, its slime frozen into hard plates of ice, with sickly blue skin and eyes like sapphires.
creatures.notes:
Defense is +6 against grapples. A wyrm may grapple its own Size in Size 0 enemies. Attack Damage leaves out Constant Damaging Effect, which adds +5 when it applies. Soak is printed as 10, +12 plates of ice. No Art is printed for its vis (Ant p. 127). Its Abilities are the book's Pretenses.

Printed: the plates neutralize its poison, yet Venomous Bite is listed; the challenge says seven miles freeze, the power says one mile.
creatures.secrets:
Ice wyrms stand for the edge between arable land and the snowy north, or peak and pasture, or the draining of life by winter. This one is a mastery faerie: it must fall to humans in an epic fight that passes into local legend, and until then it hunts warm life to drain (Ant p. 127).

The Queen's servants catch it and move it by mirror. A piece of the frame lies in its treasure.

creatures.name: Smoothface (Basic Soldier)

powers.name: Gripping Fear
powers.description: Constant. Humans who see the smooth face are seized by terror and flee, losing Fatigue. Several may ambush a resting victim together, or one may torment it alone with Invisibility and Shift Human Shapes. As Panic of the Trembling Heart, ArM5 p. 148, +1 constant, +2 intricacy points to cut the cost; also printed as ReMe Base 5, +1 Eye, +2 Sun, +2 intricacy.

powers.name: Invisibility
powers.description: A personal Veil of Invisibility, ArM5 p. 146.

powers.name: Loss of Sense of Direction
powers.description: A version of Guide, turning a fleeing victim toward some deserted spot for another attack.

powers.name: Shift Human Shapes
powers.description: It wipes its face away with a hand, or back again, and takes other human forms: invisibly it catches a spent human, comes as a comfort and scares him afresh. Base 3, +2 Sun, +1 intricacy point to cut cost, though its Duration is Mom.

creatures.appearance: Altogether human until it pleases, when one stroke leaves skin as bare and white as an eggshell, which still sees and smells.
creatures.notes:
Wounds as printed: 0, -1 (1-5), -1 (6-10), -3 (11-15), -5 (16-20), Incapacitated (21-25), Dead (26+). Soak includes full metal scale armor (Ant p. 126). Its Abilities are the book's Pretenses.

A template: take the character it is pretending to be, then add 10 Might, these Virtues and Flaws (or Infiltrator where it suits), Personality Traits, Powers and Vis. This example is the Basic Soldier of ArM5 p. 22. As a player character it needs higher Characteristics and six Minor Flaws, and may want the Damaging Effect power (p. 126).
creatures.secrets:
They haunt travellers and those who fear strangers, for sport and vitality. One who frightens a victim to death may wear that face. They fight only to defend themselves (Ant p. 126).

In the Herbam challenge they mean to keep the Gifted child, hoping it will draw faces for them. They hate mirrors and the Queen hates them; they know nothing of her, but may be persuaded that she has put them in peril with her gift, and side with the magi at the end (pp. 126-127).

creatures.name: Knockers

powers.name: Guide
powers.description: Nudges people toward a course of action: it rewards good miners with warnings or the way to ore, and sends bad ones astray or into peril. Base 5, +2 Voice, +1 Conc, +2 Group.

powers.name: Loosely Material
powers.description: Forms a solid body for a time, with all its gear. 2 intricacy points cut the Might cost.

creatures.appearance: Small, insubstantial dwarfs in miners' gear, who pass for the ghosts of Jewish miners killed underground. They cast no reflection.
creatures.notes:
Combat totals include +1 for a Pretense specialization. Soak is printed +6, with Immunity from Terram (Ant p. 129). No Art is printed for the vis. Its Abilities are the book's Pretenses.

They warn of cave-ins with their noise, and lead men to good ore by tapping. They count whistling very rude. They are sincerely religious, and cannot hold on to the riddle of why death made them dwarfs for more than a moment.
creatures.secrets:
They bargain gladly if approached in peace, above all with miners and Jews. They give up the child for binding oaths that it be properly raised; break those, and they may undermine the covenant, shift its underground waters or find other revenges (Ant p. 129).

Having no reflection, they have no use for mirrors, and they know much about the Queen. Even attacked, they can give away her weakness: they fight a few rounds with tools and mirrors, cry out that the mirrors have failed them, and flee through tunnels or rock.

creatures.name: The Waimie

params.power: Two Heads Are Better Than One
must bite to use The Envenomed Gift

powers.name: Constriction
powers.description: Non-magical. She can constrict only a victim smaller than she is, by the grappling rules (ArM5 p. 174). While she holds the grapple the victim counts as deprived of air (ArM5 p. 180) and makes a Stamina check every five rounds or takes the usual effects. Once a grapple is established she can keep constricting and still bite, at the held victim or at someone else. (p. 134)

powers.name: The Envenomed Gift
powers.description: On top of the ordinary venom she may choose to taint the Gift of anyone she bites, who suffers the Painful Magic Flaw for a day. No Hermetic equivalent. Greater Power x 2 (50 levels, -5 Might cost, +5 Init). The book prints the word Init with no figure after it, so the Initiative here is left at 0. (p. 134)

powers.name: Serpent Spies
powers.description: With a touch she links her mind to one of her children and sees and hears all that the young serpent does. She can hold any number of these links at once, and each lasts until she drops it, but the Might spent on a link does not return until then. Printed as Init Qik -4. InAn 40 (Base 15, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 extra sense, +1 constant). Greater Power (40 levels, -2 Might cost). (pp. 134-135)

powers.name: Scion of the World Serpent
powers.description: She swells to any Size from one above her present Size up to +12, with +2 Strength and -1 Quickness per point of Size and new wound ranges. Size +9 is 130 feet long and six feet thick, +10 is 170 by seven, +11 is 210 by ten, and +12 is 265 by thirteen. It must be renewed at sunrise and sunset and may lapse if she is distracted then. While it lasts her natural attacks are magical and must Penetrate Magic Resistance; Animal spells still use her original Size. MuAn 30 (Base 4, +2 Sun, +4 Size to affect Size +12). Personal Power x 2 (30 levels, -3 Might cost, +1 Init). (p. 135)

powers.name: Swallow Whole
powers.description: Non-magical. She can swallow anything at least 5 Size points smaller than she is. A creature not first subdued by Constriction may struggle, but stays constricted while swallowed. No one can breathe inside her, so deprivation rolls (ArM5 p. 180) apply even after escaping the grapple. Three rounds later the victim reaches the stomach: acid does +9 damage a round, or +36 at full immersion (ArM5 p. 181). A Strength + Athletics roll each round may brace him: Ease Factor 6 for half immersion (triple damage), 9 for one limb (double), 12 for a splash (normal). She swallows no second creature until the first reaches the stomach. (p. 135)

powers.name: Two Heads Are Better Than One
powers.description: Costs 1 or more points. Her head splits lengthwise into two or more, one more per extra Might point, each giving another attack. She fights as a trained group of as many as she has heads, with no Leadership limit on the Group bonus. Physical attacks made with this power must Penetrate Magic Resistance. MuAn 50 (Base 25, +2 Sun, +3 Size). Greater Power (50 levels, -4 Might cost and +1 Init from Improved Powers). (p. 135)

powers.name: Venomous Bite
powers.description: Non-magical. Compare her Attack Advantage with the victim's armor Protection, not his Soak: if hers is higher, he takes the effects of adder venom (Poison Table, ArM5 p. 180), wounded or not. (p. 135)

creatures.appearance: A monstrous legless, wingless dragon of a serpent, 130 feet from end to end and more than six feet through at the widest. Each horny scale carries a ridge drawn out into a spine lying flat along the body, and snake's scutes run down her belly. The head is eight feet long and wedge-shaped, hooked at the tip, with curved fangs. She is a blotched green, darker along the back and paler toward the belly, and she speaks in a whisper that trembles over a forked tongue.
creatures.notes:
Wound ranges: Light 1-14, Medium to 28, Heavy to 42, Incapacitated to 56, Dead from 57.

Printed Magic Lore 5+2: the +2 is Student of Magic. Serpent is her Essential Trait. Her block gives Fatigue levels OK, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious.

Pronounced WAY-mee. It is the word of northern England and southern Scotland for a worm, in the sense of a dragon. Elsewhere she takes another name: the Orm in northern Europe, the Wivere where French is spoken, the Suge among the Basques, the Mengue in Cantabria, the Hudra among the Greeks, and perhaps the Lindwurm in the Rhine Tribunal. (p. 134)

What the valley tells. A century ago, they say, a sinner fishing on a Sunday caught an eel-like thing and threw it down a well. It grew. Milk sated its hunger for livestock, until the valley's one dairy farmer could not keep up, and each wound it took from the knights closed with its own blood. A champion in armor set with blades faced it astride a river and it cut itself apart in his grip; the river carried off the blood, and every piece became a small serpent waiting to be fished out on a Sunday. One old man holds instead that its hide was proof against everything, and that it died of burning peat thrust down its throat on a spear, new serpents rising where the burning blood fell on marjoram. A third swears it was a princess cursed by her stepmother and freed by her brother, and that the curse rebounded on the witch, who haunts the land with her brood still. (pp. 137-138)

Add the aura modifier to Magic Resistance and subtract the Magic Sensitivity score. A Quality or Inferiority that changes a Magic Animal's Size leaves its Might alone, as Size comes off Might before Qualities are bought (Realms of Power: Magic pp. 30-36); a change of Size by a Virtue or Flaw does alter Might. The book offers this as a clarification. (pp. 134-135)
creatures.secrets:
An ancient creature of the Magic Realm, and very strong for it. She needs vis to hold what she has learned and to grow, so she bears serpents without end and sends them to fetch it. She feels little for them. Most die in the crush of siblings; those that live often lose ground to Acclimation as they grow. (p. 133)

She keeps half the year in the Magic Realm, sharing her cave with whichever child is least stupid. She spies through her small children, and so learned of the Order and how magi hunt and hoard vis, which suggested an easier way to feed. She has no knowledge of the Aegis of the Hearth. (pp. 133, 137)

Her large daughters press her constantly, sometimes in league with younger ones, for too many survivors try to kill her and mother broods of their own. (p. 133)

Blades cannot harm her. None of the tales is true, but one holds a hint of this, the book does not say which, and nothing tells the characters so. (p. 138)

In her insula each wound she takes bleeds a living serpent into the fight on her side: a one-year-old from a Light Wound, a three-year-old from a Medium, a five-year-old from a Heavy or Incapacitating. These do not spawn in turn when hurt. She hides among the mounds and strikes by surprise, and a harder fight adds her offspring of six to eight years. (p. 140)

A weaker Waimie: use one of the brood as the mother, and slow them to two or more years per step. Or alternate the yearly 5 Might with 5 points of Inferiorities: Minor Flaw (Anchored to (Land), Baneful Circumstances, Clumsy, Environmental Sensitivity, Essential Flaw, (Form) Monstrosity, Lesser Malediction or Poor Characteristic), Reduced Attack, Reduced Might or Reduced Powers; some are in Realms of Power: Magic pp. 47-51. (p. 135)

A stronger Waimie: give her human servants, the Cult of the Serpent, held perhaps by something like Entrancement. Without Difficult Underlings she can send her children in coordinated groups, and if she beats the magi outright she need share no vis source with her brood. (p. 136)

creatures.appearance: To look at, a man, and a much smaller thing than his wife.

creatures.secrets: The father of the brood. creatures.notes: An elder daughter of the Waimie. The book names no age and prints no block of her own: use the brood block that suits.
creatures.secrets: If the characters are not at once hostile to the brood, she looks to them for freedom. Her mother shuts the eldest out of the Magic Realm cave, so that Acclimation stunts them and they can neither challenge her nor brood, which needs a serpent of the mother's size. Some eat their kin for the vis; some roam far for it, and it is barely enough. She needs a Magic aura strong enough to stop Acclimation, and a mate that is near enough serpent or dragon.

creatures.name: St. John the Apostle

powers.name: Curse of Drowning
powers.description: As the Hand of St. John's power (p. 52): the target vomits sea water and drowns, unable to act, making Deprivation rolls every 30 seconds until the wielder stops.

powers.name: Grant Visions
powers.description: A true vision of the future, clouded in mystical allegory. Intelligence + Divine Lore against Ease Factor 9 gives a rough reading; a higher roll reveals more.

powers.name: Heal Burns
powers.description: Heals any non-lethal wound caused by fire.

powers.name: Purge Poison
powers.description: The target vomits the poison up, is healed of any non-lethal wound or fatigue from it, and takes no more damage.

powers.name: Turn Back the Missile
powers.description: As the Hand of St. John's power (p. 52), of the appropriate Form: missiles are hurled back at those who sent them.

creatures.appearance: Shown in art with a chalice and serpent, a book, or an eagle.
creatures.notes:
Areas of veneration: authors, booksellers, friendships, against burns and poisoning, and tanners. Feast: December 27.

He also has Expel Demons, Ignis Domini, Raise the Dead and Terrify the Unbeliever, whose figures this book does not print; see RoP: The Divine Revised Edition.

Invoked by Bishop Orris (p. 60) under RoP: The Divine Revised Edition p. 87, and by humiliating his relic under RoP: The Divine pp. 87-88. If moved, he strikes with Curse of Drowning or Ignis Domini.

creatures.name: Nightwing
creatures.appearance: A raven with an unnatural intelligence shining in its eyes.
creatures.notes:
The Raven of Virtue, Galerius's familiar. Base statistics before the bond are in Realms of Power: Magic p. 62. Wounds -1 (1), -3 (2), -5 (3), Incapacitated (4), Dead (5+). Warping Score 1 (8).

Cords: Gold 0, Silver 3, Bronze 0. Bond powers: Mental Communication (complex), the Level 15 effect of ArM5 p. 105, working for both partners; Shared Senses, the Level 30 effect of ArM5 p. 105, letting Galerius use Nightwing's senses but not the reverse.
creatures.secrets: Galerius sees and hears through the raven to watch places and scout, and if he learns he is being followed it serves as his lookout. The raven is also a clue to his approach: seen once, it is watched for, and ordinary ravens can keep the magi on edge (pp. 72, 75, 77).

creatures.name: Hannelore, Vengeful Ghost

powers.name: Betrayal of the Heart
powers.description: Each use shows her one fact about the target that he would never admit, drawn from his secret fears and sins. The truly holy may be immune, having no secrets however small.

powers.name: Envisioning
powers.description: For 1 point she enters a sleeper's dreams; she cannot change them at a stroke but can slowly darken them and speak through any figure in them. For 5 points she forces a waking vision of whatever she likes, which may stun for a round, and the victim needs a Brave roll of 9+ to avoid retching, convulsions or terror. It is her only way of speaking to humans.

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: 1 to 3 points. When a mortal indulges a venial sin she may impose her Obsession Traits, Infatuation or Revenge; if it penetrates, sinful thoughts assail him and he gains the Trait at the points spent, which may stick if he indulges again at his next chance. RoP: Infernal pp. 31-32.

powers.name: Possession
powers.description: Variable points. Any Might she spends becomes a Possession Might Pool inside the victim, not regained until the possession ends; more does more with the host but penetrates less. If it overcomes resistance she controls him directly. RoP: Infernal p. 32.

powers.name: Whispers Behind the Back
powers.description: Exactly as the spell Pains of the Perpetual Worry: a month's nagging dread, tied to the victim's secret sins, that everyone knows and talks behind his back.

creatures.appearance: As in life, but her face is pinched into a caricature of itself and her skin scarlet as if boiled. Small horns show in her tousled hair, and her faded fine clothes stream behind her as if blown by a furnace wind.
creatures.notes:
Virtues, Flaws and Abilities as in life; her diabolist block is entered. Wounds -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+). The book gives no Hierarchy Score here.

Incorporeal in her natural form, with no power to form a solid body, so only a spirit can fight her physically.

The storyguide may raise her Might: her Infernal Reputation could make her a Master or Lord, +5 or +10. Whether she keeps her maleficia as a demon is left open.
creatures.secrets: Hell lets her back, with her punishment eased a little for each soul won. She has a year from the anniversary of her death to win one, tempting it to mortal sin and seeing it die unrepentant; each success gives another year. Possessed humans pass an Aegis unless the demon extends its Magic Resistance over the host (RoP: Infernal p. 32), but if the Aegis's Penetration beats her Infernal Might all powers cost double. She flees superior force. If she sees her beloved she cannot help dropping her plans to kill him (p. 94).

It stays in the background, using Hannelore on Earth. Watchers specialize in teaching corrupt magic and are among the most powerful demons outside Hell, patient beyond most of their kind for a time. Combat: dagger Init +1, Attack +5, Defense +4, Damage +2. Soak -1. Fatigue levels OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wounds -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Equipment: fine clothes. Encumbrance 0 (0).

Appearance: a girl on the edge of womanhood, very pretty, with dark wavy hair and deep green eyes. She talks about philosophy with an eagerness thought unsuited to her rank.

One Flaw point more than Virtues at this age; the Protection Virtue would probably have balanced it had she not gone the way she does (p. 86).

character.summary:
The favoured daughter of Baron Hugo, raised in comfort by a doting father and taught by private tutors, who noticed her temper and ambition and prayed for whoever marries her. She is educated, eloquent and sure of herself, and the Gift does not trouble her. She loves hawking and courtly romances.

She has never married. Those proposed for her fall ill, meet with accidents or disappear, and people find they cannot bear to stay long in her company.
character.secrets:
Attracted to power, she reads the jealousy the Gift stirs as power's natural effect, and fixes on a magus who seems strong (p. 85). She is infatuated with him and his power; he may love her, she does not love him. Her target is best not repulsive, and need not be a man. Variants: avarice (she wants to be taught, impossible without the Gift) or envy (she wants his magic from him); a male Hannelore; a same-sex pursuit, kept secret, where Hugo might seek no clemency; a companion or storyguide character as target, whom she can enslave and later curse at Arcane Range from connections taken while she held him, watching in crow form if he dwells within an Aegis; a weaker version, with a Power or her vis taken away, keeping Diablerie; a stronger one, with a coven, demons and corrupted beasts in pact, or more Powers; a one-time threat with no prior romance, going straight to her death and return (pp. 80, 84-85).

From a block of forbidden books she initiated herself into the Unholy Method of Incantation, at the cost of a Warping point. The rite drew a powerful demon in a pleasing form, who taught her for five years, feeding her instability with its Obsession power. She knows her power is illicit but does not at first know it is Infernal, or that her beloved's is not (p. 87). She has more Virtues than creation allows: demonic tutelage equal to Mentored by Demons five times (RoP: Infernal p. 86), 50 extra experience a year, and Vituperations that gave her Self-Confident and Aging Points. Such an outlay suggests Hell plans more for her, and that the infatuation is a distraction (p. 81).

Hierarchy Score 3. Fragile Constitution, Infernal Blessing and Tainted With Evil come from Warping, and Arcane Lore free with Diabolist. Her Warping is so high because she takes Warping to fuel her magic (RoP: Infernal p. 104) and carries lasting effects. Unaffected by The Gift: RoP: Magic p. 47 (p. 81).

Powers from her Infernal Blessing, a Level 25 Debauchery / Phantasm effect (Base 4, +1 Touch, +4 Forsaken) (p. 81). Gaze of the Wolf: with eye contact she fixes a person in place while she holds the stare; Penetration 5 + Penetration Bonus + Aura Modifier. The text calls this her Transfix power (pp. 83, 88). Exhaustion: her touch inflicts a Long-Term Fatigue level; not in the Dominion or on women; Penetration as above.

Her vis (p. 81): at least 3 + simple die pawns at any time, some turned to vis prava. Not Personal Vis Sources, as it is never automatic. She steals the Host at Communion and profanes it (RoP: Infernal p. 96); has replaced the relic in her father's chapel with a fake and profaned the true one; contests the spring's vis; and has the beads on one book of her father's.

Casting (p. 82): Communication + Incantation + Power + Aura modifier + stress die. Her Hierarchy spares her the harsh effects of a failed maleficium of level 30 or below. Each use costs a Confidence point, adding nothing, or a Warping point. Range Personal, Duration Forsaken maleficia are taken as already cast (And the Devil, Black Wings, She Who Bears the Mark); each gives a Warping point a year, not included in her score. Bonuses: +5 a pawn of vis prava or +2 of other vis (at most Incantation + Power pawns); +3 a Confidence point (at most 2); +6 for sacrificing a black animal; +5 an assistant at Communication +1 and Incantation 4 (at most 3 with Diablerie, 2 otherwise). With Diablerie, her best Power, around 53 + stress die with Infernal aura 2, 2 Confidence, 4 pawns of vis prava and a black goat; +15 with a coven of 3. See RoP: Infernal chapter 10.

Her maleficia (pp. 82-83) are not formulaic, and she may vary Range, Duration, Target or effect:
A Crown of Twelve Stars on Her Head (Psychomachia, level 40; R Voice, D Moon, T Ind; Base 15, +2 Voice, +3 Moon): the target obeys her commands for the duration, but must be able to see her, hear her voice or smell her perfume, or it ends at once. Usually laid with vis and a sacrifice on a victim she already holds.
A Ghost on the Wind I Shall Become / No Door Can Stop Me (Diablerie, 45; R Per, D Sun, T Ind; Base 35, +2 Sun): the Nightwalker Major Virtue (Hedge Magic Revised Edition p. 104) until sunrise. Her spirit leaves her prone body and travels at great speed, changing between corporeal and immaterial in three rounds, and invisible at will when immaterial. Corporeal she can lift what she could normally carry, which then goes immaterial with her. People near her spirit grow drowsy, and sleepers cannot be woken. Spells on ghosts or spirits affect her, but with no Might she cannot be warded off or laid to rest. She cannot enter the Dominion so.
And the Devil Shall Take Care of His Own (Diablerie, 40; R Per, D Forsaken, T Ind; base effect, +4 Forsaken): Magic Resistance 25, not stacking with other sources.
Black Wings, Eye-Piercing Beak (Diablerie, 35; R Per, D Forsaken, T Ind; Base 15, +4 Forsaken): a False Power copying Skinchanger, crow shape. Her focal item is a fetish made of the wings of the bird she sacrificed.
Blood and Body of the Beast (Diablerie, 35; R Touch, D Mom, T Ind; Base 30, +1 Touch): a short mockery of the Eucharist turning a pawn of vis to vis prava (RoP: Infernal p. 19), worth +5 a pawn to her, not +2.
Break Not, Bend Not, Burn Not / Thy Powers Desert (Diablerie, 25; R Touch, D Sun, T Ind; base effect, +1 Touch, +2 Sun): one object, not living and no larger than a base Individual of its Form, gains Magic Resistance 15, not stacking.
Clothed in the Dragon's Scales (Diablerie, 50; R Per, D Moon, T Ind; Base 35, +3 Moon): a False Power copying Greater Immunity, chosen for the peril, fire being the obvious one. Its level means she can really try only once, with a heavy sacrifice, much vis or a good Ceremony bonus. Could she reach level 55 she would make it Forsaken.
Her Iniquities Shall Be Hidden From His Eyes (Psychomachia, 25; R Eye, D Moon, T Ind; Level 5, +1 Eye, +3 Moon): the target mistakes one thing for something else, a man for a serving maid, a malefic casting for a country dance.
Mother Lilith, Queen of Desire / Stroke his Staff, Stoke the Fire (Psychomachia, 25; R Eye, D Sun, T Ind; Base 10, +1 Eye, +2 Sun): burning lust. She cannot direct the victim but can work him like an addict. Usually follows her power to hold him still.
Pact of the Chalice of Blood (Diablerie, 25; R Voice, D Moon, T Ind; Base 4, +2 Voice, +3 Moon): solemnizes an uncoerced pact with an intelligent creature of Infernal Might, both drinking a sacrifice's blood; it must keep the terms to the letter. Such as a Fimus (RoP: Infernal p. 68), a Fictilis (p. 69) or Morrighu (pp. 72-73) are within her power.
She Who Bears the Mark Shall Be Unharmed (Diablerie, 35; R Per, D Forsaken, T Ind; Base 15, +4 Forsaken): a False Power copying Lesser Immunity, perhaps several times over, to long swords or another weapon, or to magical fire or the like. Each costs resources and Warping, so she may leave a gap; she has likely not guarded against her love's favourite magic, thinking he would never attack her.
The Scorched Heart of a Man Obsessed (Malediction, 35; R Eye, D Moon, T Ind; Base 15, +1 Eye, +3 Moon): the Obsessed Flaw, fixed on her. Near her he can only attend on her; away, she fills his thoughts. Often laid once she has already bewitched him.
The Wrath of Woman Scorches the Valor of Man (Malediction, 35; R Voice, D Sun, T Ind; Base 15, +2 Voice, +2 Sun): overwhelming Fear of women, as the Flaw.
Thy Health Shall Shrivel Like Straw in a Flame (Malediction, 30; R Eye, D Sun, T Ind; Level 5, +1 Eye, +2 Sun, +1 extra point, +1 to lower the minimum): Stamina down 2, to no less than -1, with sudden pain and a hacking cough, trembling heart or other small ailment for the duration.
Trampled Under Death's Pale Hooves (Malediction, 30; R Eye, D Sun, T Ind; base effect, +1 Eye, +2 Sun): -6 to all Ride rolls and 6 extra botch dice on a 0. This and its like for other Abilities are how she disposes of unwanted suitors.

Tactics (pp. 88-90): a maleficium is very obvious, all chanted blasphemies, so she uses Gaze of the Wolf first unless she has surprise. She times incantations for sunrise or sunset, when the Parma Magica lapses. She is no match for a group of magi, with low Penetration against those she has no interest in, but curses companions and grogs with Minor Flaws such as Noncombatant, Palsied Hands or Fear, or blights an Ability or Characteristic, all deliverable at Duration Diameter. She fights hit and run from spirit form, leaves in crow shape, and may bring minor demons under a pact, or a former suitor ensorceled with A Crown of Twelve Stars. His name, and any letters in his own hand, are sympathetic connections she holds to her love.

Redemption (p. 89): she is not beyond it. A patient character, perhaps with the baron, may bring her to see the source of her power and give it up. Abandoned after a true wish to repent, she relapses and seeks revenge. Her wish will be tested by God and fought by her patron; penance means a nunnery.
